1.58.s: ..sūta uvāca ..
1.58.d: ॥सूत उवाच ॥
1.58.m:
The Sūta said:
Hereafter I shall declare again the ordinance of the Dvāpara.
There, when the Tretāyuga has waned, the Dvāpara begins.

1.58.s:
ata ūrddhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi dvāparasya vidhiṃ punaḥ.
tatra tretāyuge kṣīṇe dvāparaṃ pratipadyate .. 58.1 ..
1.58.d:
अत ऊर्द्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि द्वापरस्य विधिं पुनः।
तत्र त्रेतायुगे क्षीणे द्वापरं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 58.1 ॥

1.58.s:
dvāparādau prajānāntu siddhistratāyuge tu yā.
parivṛtte yuge tasmiṃstataḥ sā saṃpraṇaśyati .. 58.2 ..
1.58.d:
द्वापरादौ प्रजानान्तु सिद्धिस्त्रतायुगे तु या।
परिवृत्ते युगे तस्मिंस्ततः सा संप्रणश्यति ॥ 58.2 ॥
1.58.m: At the beginning of Dvāpara, whatever perfection belonged to creatures in the Tretā yuga— / when that yuga turns, that [perfection] is then completely destroyed.

1.58.s:
tataḥ pravarttate tāsāṃ prajānāṃ dvāpare punaḥ.
lobho'dhṛtirvaṇigyuddhaṃ tattvānāmaviniścayaḥ .. 58.3 ..
1.58.d:
ततः प्रवर्त्तते तासां प्रजानां द्वापरे पुनः।
लोभोऽधृतिर्वणिग्युद्धं तत्त्वानामविनिश्चयः ॥ 58.3 ॥
1.58.m: Then, among those creatures in Dvāpara, there arise again / greed, discontent, commerce, warfare, and uncertainty regarding truths,

1.58.s:
tambhedaścaiva varṇānāṃ kāryāṇāñcā vinirṇayaḥ.
yajñauṣadheḥ paśordaṇḍo mado dambho'kṣamā balam.
eṣāṃ rajastamoyuktā pravṛttirdvāpare smṛtā .. 58.4 ..
1.58.d:
तम्भेदश्चैव वर्णानां कार्याणाञ्चा विनिर्णयः।
यज्ञौषधेः पशोर्दण्डो मदो दम्भोऽक्षमा बलम्।
एषां रजस्तमोयुक्ता प्रवृत्तिर्द्वापरे स्मृता ॥ 58.4 ॥
1.58.m: confusion of the social classes, indecision regarding duties, / violence toward sacrificial plants and beasts, arrogance, deceit, intolerance, and brute force. / Their activity in Dvāpara is remembered as being associated with rajas and tamas.

1.58.s:
ādye kṛte ca dharmo'sti tretāyāṃ samprapadyate.
dvāpare vyākulībhūtvā praṇaśyati kalau yuge .. 58.5 ..
1.58.d:
आद्ये कृते च धर्मोऽस्ति त्रेतायां सम्प्रपद्यते।
द्वापरे व्याकुलीभूत्वा प्रणश्यति कलौ युगे ॥ 58.5 ॥
1.58.m: In the initial Kṛta [yuga] there is dharma; in Tretā it is attained; / becoming confused in Dvāpara, it perishes in the Kali yuga.

1.58.s:
varṇānāṃ viparidhvaṃsaḥ saṃkīrttyate tathāśramaḥ.
dvaidhamutpadyate caiva yuge tasmin śrutau smṛtau .. 58.6 ..
1.58.d:
वर्णानां विपरिध्वंसः संकीर्त्त्यते तथाश्रमः।
द्वैधमुत्पद्यते चैव युगे तस्मिन् श्रुतौ स्मृतौ ॥ 58.6 ॥
1.58.m: The ruination of the social classes and the stages of life is recounted; / and division arises in that yuga in both Śruti and Smṛti.

1.58.s:
dvaidhāt śruteḥ smṛteścaiva niścayo nādhigamyate.
aniścayādigamanāddharmatattvaṃ nigadyate.
dharmatattve tu bhinnānāṃ matibhedo bhavennṛṇām .. 58.7 ..
1.58.d:
द्वैधात् श्रुतेः स्मृतेश्चैव निश्चयो नाधिगम्यते।
अनिश्चयादिगमनाद्धर्मतत्त्वं निगद्यते।
धर्मतत्त्वे तु भिन्नानां मतिभेदो भवेन्नृणाम् ॥ 58.7 ॥
1.58.m: Because of division in revelation and tradition, no certainty is attained. / From the lack of certainty [about the goal], the essential truth of dharma is proclaimed [differently]. / And when the essential truth of dharma is divided, men have divergent opinions.

1.58.s:
parasparavibhinnaistairdṛṣṭīnāṃ vibhrameṇa ca.
ayaṃ dharmo hyayaṃ neti niścayo nābhigamyate .. 58.8 ..
1.58.d:
परस्परविभिन्नैस्तैर्दृष्टीनां विभ्रमेण च।
अयं धर्मो ह्ययं नेति निश्चयो नाभिगम्यते ॥ 58.8 ॥
1.58.m: Because they are mutually divided and because of error in their views, / no certainty is attained: 'This indeed is dharma; this is not.'

1.58.s:
kāraṇānāñca vakailyāt kāraṇasyāpyaniścayāt.
matibhede ca teṣāṃ vai dṛṣṭīnāṃ vibhramo bhavet .. 58.9 ..
1.58.d:
कारणानाञ्च वकैल्यात् कारणस्याप्यनिश्चयात्।
मतिभेदे च तेषां वै दृष्टीनां विभ्रमो भवेत् ॥ 58.9 ॥
1.58.m: From deficiency of reasons, and from uncertainty about the cause itself, / when they hold divergent opinions, there arises error in their views.

1.58.s:
tato dṛṣṭivibhinnaistaiḥ kṛtaṃ śāstrakulantvidam.
eko vedaśvatuṣpādastretāsviha vidhīyate .. 58.10 ..
1.58.d:
ततो दृष्टिविभिन्नैस्तैः कृतं शास्त्रकुलन्त्विदम्।
एको वेदश्वतुष्पादस्त्रेतास्विह विधीयते ॥ 58.10 ॥
1.58.m: Then, divided in their views, they produced this multitude of scriptures. / Here in the Tretā ages the Veda is ordained as one, with four quarters.

1.58.s:
saṃrodhādāyuṣaścaiva dṛśyate dvāpareṣu ca .
vedavyāsaiścaturdhā tu vyasyate dvāparādiṣu .. 58.11 ..
1.58.d:
संरोधादायुषश्चैव दृश्यते द्वापरेषु च ।
वेदव्यासैश्चतुर्धा तु व्यस्यते द्वापरादिषु ॥ 58.11 ॥
1.58.m: And in the Dvāparas it is seen [divided] because of the curtailment of lifespan; / for by the compilers of the Veda it is divided fourfold in the Dvāparas and other [ages].

1.58.s:
ṛṣiputraiḥ punarvedā bhidyante dṛṣṭivibhramaiḥ.
mantrabrāhmaṇavinyāsaiḥ svaravarṇaviparyayaiḥ .. 58.12 ..
1.58.d:
ऋषिपुत्रैः पुनर्वेदा भिद्यन्ते दृष्टिविभ्रमैः।
मन्त्रब्राह्मणविन्यासैः स्वरवर्णविपर्ययैः ॥ 58.12 ॥
1.58.m: The Vedas are further split up by the sons of seers through errors in their views, / by arrangements of mantras and Brāhmaṇas, and by reversals of accents and syllables.

1.58.s:
saṃhitā ṛgyajuḥsāmnāṃ saṃhanyante śrutarṣibhiḥ.
sāmānyādvaikṛtāccaiva dṛṣṭibhinnaiḥ vkacitvkacit .. 58.13 ..
1.58.d:
संहिता ऋग्यजुःसाम्नां संहन्यन्ते श्रुतर्षिभिः।
सामान्याद्वैकृताच्चैव दृष्टिभिन्नैः व्कचित्व्कचित् ॥ 58.13 ॥
1.58.m: Saṃhitās of Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman are compiled by the learned seers, / by those whose views are divided here and there, based on the general and the modified [rules].

1.58.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ kalpasūtrāṇi mantrapravacanāni ca.
anye tu prahitāstīrthaiḥ kecittān pratyavasthitāḥ .. 58.14 ..
1.58.d:
ब्राह्मणं कल्पसूत्राणि मन्त्रप्रवचनानि च।
अन्ये तु प्रहितास्तीर्थैः केचित्तान् प्रत्यवस्थिताः ॥ 58.14 ॥
1.58.m: Brāhmaṇa texts, Kalpasūtras, and recitations of mantras [are composed]. / Some are sent forth by the orthodox traditions; others stand opposed to them.

1.58.s:
dvāpareṣu pravarttante bhinnavṛttāśramā dvijāḥ.
ekamādhvaryavaṃ pūrvamāsīddvaidhaṃ punastataḥ .. 58.15 ..
1.58.d:
द्वापरेषु प्रवर्त्तन्ते भिन्नवृत्ताश्रमा द्विजाः।
एकमाध्वर्यवं पूर्वमासीद्द्वैधं पुनस्ततः ॥ 58.15 ॥
1.58.m: In the Dvāparas, twice-born men arise whose conduct and stages of life are divided. / Formerly the office of the Adhvaryu was single; then it became twofold again.

1.58.s:
sāmānyaviparītārthaiḥ kṛtaṃ śāstrakulantvidam.
ādhvaryavasya prastāvairbahudhā vyākulaṃ kṛtam .. 58.16 ..
1.58.d:
सामान्यविपरीतार्थैः कृतं शास्त्रकुलन्त्विदम्।
आध्वर्यवस्य प्रस्तावैर्बहुधा व्याकुलं कृतम् ॥ 58.16 ॥
1.58.m: This multitude of scriptures was made with common and contrary meanings; / it was made greatly confused by introductions to the office of the Adhvaryu.

1.58.s:
tathaivātharvaṛksāmnāṃ vikalpaiścāpyasaṃkṣayaiḥ.
vyākulaṃ dvāpare bhinne kriyate bhinnadarśanaiḥ .. 58.17 ..
1.58.d:
तथैवाथर्वऋक्साम्नां विकल्पैश्चाप्यसंक्षयैः।
व्याकुलं द्वापरे भिन्ने क्रियते भिन्नदर्शनैः ॥ 58.17 ॥
1.58.m: Likewise, through endless variations in the Atharvan, Ṛg, and Sāman, / it is made confused in the divided Dvāpara by men of divergent views.

1.58.s:
taiṣāṃ bhedāḥ prabhedāśca vikalpaiścāpyasaṃkṣayāḥ .
dvāpare sampravartante vinaśyanti punaḥ kalau .. 58.18 ..
1.58.d:
तैषां भेदाः प्रभेदाश्च विकल्पैश्चाप्यसंक्षयाः ।
द्वापरे सम्प्रवर्तन्ते विनश्यन्ति पुनः कलौ ॥ 58.18 ॥
1.58.m: Their divisions and subdivisions, endless through variations, / arise in the Dvāpara and perish again in the Kali [age].

1.58.s:
teṣāṃ viparyayāścaiva bhavanti dvāpare punaḥ.
avṛṣṭirmaraṇañcaiva tathaiva vyādhyupadvavāḥ .. 58.19 ..
1.58.d:
तेषां विपर्ययाश्चैव भवन्ति द्वापरे पुनः।
अवृष्टिर्मरणञ्चैव तथैव व्याध्युपद्ववाः ॥ 58.19 ॥
1.58.m: And their reversals occur again in the Dvāpara: / drought, death, and likewise calamities from disease.

1.58.s:
vāṅmanaḥkarmajairduḥkhairnirvedo jāyate punaḥ .
nirvedājjāyate teṣāṃ duḥkhamokṣa vicāraṇā .. 58.20 ..
1.58.d:
वाङ्मनःकर्मजैर्दुःखैर्निर्वेदो जायते पुनः ।
निर्वेदाज्जायते तेषां दुःखमोक्ष विचारणा ॥ 58.20 ॥
1.58.m: From sufferings born of speech, mind, and action, world-weariness arises again; / from world-weariness arises their inquiry into liberation from suffering.

1.58.s:
vicārāṇācca vairāgyaṃ vairāgyāddopadarśanam.
doṣāṇāṃ darśanāccaiva dvāpare jñānasambhavaḥ .. 58.21 ..
1.58.d:
विचाराणाच्च वैराग्यं वैराग्याद्दोपदर्शनम्।
दोषाणां दर्शनाच्चैव द्वापरे ज्ञानसम्भवः ॥ 58.21 ॥
1.58.m: From inquiry comes detachment, and from detachment the seeing of defects; / and from the seeing of defects knowledge arises in the Dvāpara.

1.58.s:
teṣāñca mānināṃ pūrvamādye svāyambhuve'ntare.
utpadyante hi śāstrāṇāṃ dvāpare paripanthinaḥ .. 58.22 ..
1.58.d:
तेषाञ्च मानिनां पूर्वमाद्ये स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे।
उत्पद्यन्ते हि शास्त्राणां द्वापरे परिपन्थिनः ॥ 58.22 ॥
1.58.m: And of those conceited ones formerly in the first Svāyambhuva manvantara, / opponents of the scriptures indeed arise in the Dvāpara.

1.58.s:
āyurvedavikalpāśca aṅgānāṃ jyautiṣasya ca.
arthaśāstravikalpaśca hetuśāstravikalpanam .. 58.23 ..
1.58.d:
आयुर्वेदविकल्पाश्च अङ्गानां ज्यौतिषस्य च।
अर्थशास्त्रविकल्पश्च हेतुशास्त्रविकल्पनम् ॥ 58.23 ॥
1.58.m: Variants of Āyurveda, of the Vedāṅgas, and of astronomy, / variants of the treatises on statecraft, and the invention of dialectical treatises,

1.58.s:
smṛtiśāstraprabhedāśca prasthānāni pṛthak pṛthak.
dvāpareṣvabhivarttante matibhedāstathā nṛṇām .. 58.24 ..
1.58.d:
स्मृतिशास्त्रप्रभेदाश्च प्रस्थानानि पृथक् पृथक्।
द्वापरेष्वभिवर्त्तन्ते मतिभेदास्तथा नृणाम् ॥ 58.24 ॥
1.58.m: and subdivisions of the treatises of tradition, and distinct systems of philosophy / arise in the Dvāparas, as do divergences of opinion among men.

1.58.s:
manasā karmaṇā vācā kṛcchrā dvārttā prasiddhyati.
dvāpare sarvabhūtānāṃ kāyakleśapuraskṛtā .. 58.25 ..
1.58.d:
मनसा कर्मणा वाचा कृच्छ्रा द्वार्त्ता प्रसिद्ध्यति।
द्वापरे सर्वभूतानां कायक्लेशपुरस्कृता ॥ 58.25 ॥
1.58.m: Livelihood in the Dvāpara for all beings is accomplished with difficulty / by mind, action, and speech, accompanied by physical distress.

1.58.s:
lobhe'dhṛtirvaṇigyuddhaṃ tattvānāmaviniścayaḥ.
vedaśāstrapraṇayanaṃ dharmāṇāṃ saṅkarastathā .. 58.26 ..
1.58.d:
लोभेऽधृतिर्वणिग्युद्धं तत्त्वानामविनिश्चयः।
वेदशास्त्रप्रणयनं धर्माणां सङ्करस्तथा ॥ 58.26 ॥
1.58.m: Greed, instability, trade, war, uncertainty about fundamental truths, / composition of Vedic treatises, and confusion of dharmas—

1.58.s:
dvāpareṣu pravarttante rogo lobho vadhastathā.
varṇāśramaparidhvaṃsāḥ kāmadveṣau tathaiva ca .. 58.27 ..
1.58.d:
द्वापरेषु प्रवर्त्तन्ते रोगो लोभो वधस्तथा।
वर्णाश्रमपरिध्वंसाः कामद्वेषौ तथैव च ॥ 58.27 ॥
1.58.m: disease, greed, slaughter, the ruin of castes and stages of life, / and likewise lust and hatred, arise in the Dvāparas.

1.58.s:
pūrṇe varṣasahasre dve paramāyustuthā nṛṇām.
niḥśepe dvāpare tasmin tasya sandhyā tu pādataḥ .. 58.28 ..
1.58.d:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे द्वे परमायुस्तुथा नृणाम्।
निःशेपे द्वापरे तस्मिन् तस्य सन्ध्या तु पादतः ॥ 58.28 ॥
1.58.m: Two thousand full years is the maximum lifespan of men / in that complete Dvāpara; but its twilight is a fourth part [of it].

1.58.s:
pratiṣṭhate guṇairhīno dharmo'sau dvāparasya tu .
tathaiva sandhyāpādena aṃśastasyāvatiṣṭhate .. 58.29 ..
1.58.d:
प्रतिष्ठते गुणैर्हीनो धर्मोऽसौ द्वापरस्य तु ।
तथैव सन्ध्यापादेन अंशस्तस्यावतिष्ठते ॥ 58.29 ॥
1.58.m: Deprived of virtues, that dharma of the Dvāpara stands [diminished]; / likewise its fraction abides during the twilight period.

1.58.s:
dvāparasya ca varṣe yā tiṣyasya tu nibodhata.
dvāparasyāṃśaśeṣe tu pratipattiḥ kalerataḥ .. 58.30 ..
1.58.d:
द्वापरस्य च वर्षे या तिष्यस्य तु निबोधत।
द्वापरस्यांशशेषे तु प्रतिपत्तिः कलेरतः ॥ 58.30 ॥
1.58.m: Understand now the years of the Dvāpara and of the Tiṣya [age]: / when a remaining fraction of the Dvāpara is left, the commencement of the Kali [age takes place].

1.58.s:
hiṃsāsūyānṛtaṃ māyā vadhaścaiva tapasvinām.
ete svabhāvāstiṣyasya sādhayanti ca vai prajāḥ .. 58.31 ..
1.58.d:
हिंसासूयानृतं माया वधश्चैव तपस्विनाम्।
एते स्वभावास्तिष्यस्य साधयन्ति च वै प्रजाः ॥ 58.31 ॥
1.58.m: Violence, malice, falsehood, deceit, and the slaughter of ascetics— / these are the natural traits of Tiṣya, and they overcome the creatures.

1.58.s:
eṣa dharmaḥ kṛtaḥ kṛtsno dharmaśca parihīyate.
manasā karmaṇā stutyā vārttā siddhyati vā na vā .. 58.32 ..
1.58.d:
एष धर्मः कृतः कृत्स्नो धर्मश्च परिहीयते।
मनसा कर्मणा स्तुत्या वार्त्ता सिद्ध्यति वा न वा ॥ 58.32 ॥
1.58.m: This dharma is entirely exhausted, and dharma is ruined. / Through mind, action, and praise, livelihood succeeds or fails.

1.58.s:
kalau pramārako rogaḥ satataṃ kṣudbhayāni vai.
anāvṛṣṭibhayaṃ ghoraṃ darśanañca viparyayam .. 58.33 ..
1.58.d:
कलौ प्रमारको रोगः सततं क्षुद्भयानि वै।
अनावृष्टिभयं घोरं दर्शनञ्च विपर्ययम् ॥ 58.33 ॥
1.58.m: In Kali, disease is deadly, and there are constant fears of hunger, / dreadful fear of drought, and perverted views.

1.58.s:
na pramāṇaṃ smṛterasti tiṣye loke yuge yuge.
garbhastho mriyate kaścidyauvanasthastathāparaḥ .
sthāvire madhyakaumāre mriyante vai kalau prajāḥ .. 58.34 ..
1.58.d:
न प्रमाणं स्मृतेरस्ति तिष्ये लोके युगे युगे।
गर्भस्थो म्रियते कश्चिद्यौवनस्थस्तथापरः ।
स्थाविरे मध्यकौमारे म्रियन्ते वै कलौ प्रजाः ॥ 58.34 ॥
1.58.m: There is no authority in tradition in the world in the Tiṣya yuga. / One dies in the womb, another dies in youth; / creatures die in old age, in middle age, or in childhood in Kali.

1.58.s:
adhārmikāstvanācārāstīkṣṇa kopālpatejasaḥ.
anṛtabruvaśca satataṃ tiṣye jāyanti vai prajāḥ .. 58.35 ..
1.58.d:
अधार्मिकास्त्वनाचारास्तीक्ष्ण कोपाल्पतेजसः।
अनृतब्रुवश्च सततं तिष्ये जायन्ति वै प्रजाः ॥ 58.35 ॥
1.58.m: Unrighteous, ill-behaved, fiercely angry, of little splendour, / and constantly speaking untruth are the creatures born in Tiṣya.

1.58.s:
duriṣṭairduradhītaiśca durācārairdurāgamaiḥ.
viprāṇāṃ karmadoṣaistaiḥ prajānāṃ jāyate bhayam .. 58.36 ..
1.58.d:
दुरिष्टैर्दुरधीतैश्च दुराचारैर्दुरागमैः।
विप्राणां कर्मदोषैस्तैः प्रजानां जायते भयम् ॥ 58.36 ॥
1.58.m: From bad sacrifices, bad study, bad conduct, and bad doctrines, / from these faults in the actions of Brahmins, fear arises for the subjects.

1.58.s:
hiṃsā māyā tatherṣyā ca krodho'sūyākṣamānṛtam.
tiṣye bhavanti jantūnāṃ rāgo lobhaśca sarvaśaḥ .. 58.37 ..
1.58.d:
हिंसा माया तथेर्ष्या च क्रोधोऽसूयाक्षमानृतम्।
तिष्ये भवन्ति जन्तूनां रागो लोभश्च सर्वशः ॥ 58.37 ॥
1.58.m: Violence, deceit, envy, anger, malice, impatience, and falsehood, / attachment and greed arise on all sides among creatures in Tiṣya.

1.58.s:
saṃkṣobho jāyate'tyarthaṃ kalimāsādya vai yugam.
nādhīyante tadā vedā na yajante dvijātayaḥ.
utsīdanti narāścaiva kṣatriyāḥ saviśaḥ kramāt .. 58.38 ..
1.58.d:
संक्षोभो जायतेऽत्यर्थं कलिमासाद्य वै युगम्।
नाधीयन्ते तदा वेदा न यजन्ते द्विजातयः।
उत्सीदन्ति नराश्चैव क्षत्रियाः सविशः क्रमात् ॥ 58.38 ॥
1.58.m: Great agitation arises upon reaching the Kali yuga. / The Vedas are not studied then, nor do the twice-born offer sacrifices; / and men perish, Kṣatriyas along with Vaiśyas, in due course.

1.58.s:
kṣudrāṇāmantyayonestu sambandhā brāhmaṇaiḥ saha.
bhavantīha kalau tasmin śayanāsanabhojanaiḥ .. 58.39 ..
1.58.d:
क्षुद्राणामन्त्ययोनेस्तु सम्बन्धा ब्राह्मणैः सह।
भवन्तीह कलौ तस्मिन् शयनासनभोजनैः ॥ 58.39 ॥
1.58.m: Connections of base people of the lowest birth with Brahmins / occur here in that Kali, in sleeping, sitting, and dining together.

1.58.s:
rājānaḥ śūdrabhūyiṣṭhā pāṣaṇḍānāṃ pravartakāḥ.
bhrūṇahatyāḥ prajāstatra prajā evaṃ pravarttate .. 58.40 ..
1.58.d:
राजानः शूद्रभूयिष्ठा पाषण्डानां प्रवर्तकाः।
भ्रूणहत्याः प्रजास्तत्र प्रजा एवं प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 58.40 ॥
1.58.m: Kings are mostly Śūdras, promoters of heretics; / they kill embryos in the womb; thus does mankind behave there.

1.58.s:
āyurmedhā balaṃ rūpaṃ kulañcaiva prahīyate.
śūdrāśca brāhmaṇācārāḥ śūdrācārāśca brāhmaṇāḥ .. 58.41 ..
1.58.d:
आयुर्मेधा बलं रूपं कुलञ्चैव प्रहीयते।
शूद्राश्च ब्राह्मणाचाराः शूद्राचाराश्च ब्राह्मणाः ॥ 58.41 ॥
1.58.m: Lifespan, intellect, strength, beauty, and lineage decline; / Śūdras behave like Brahmins, and Brahmins behave like Śūdras.

1.58.s:
rājavṛtte sthitāścaurāścauravṛttāśca pārthivāḥ.
bhṛtyāśca naṣṭasuhṛdo yugānte paryupasthite .. 58.42 ..
1.58.d:
राजवृत्ते स्थिताश्चौराश्चौरवृत्ताश्च पार्थिवाः।
भृत्याश्च नष्टसुहृदो युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते ॥ 58.42 ॥
1.58.m: Thieves adopt the conduct of kings, and rulers adopt the conduct of thieves; / servants lose their friends when the end of the yuga is at hand.

1.58.s:
aśīlinyo'vratāścāpi striyo madyāmiṣapriyāḥ.
māyāmātrā bhaviṣyanti yugānte pratyupasthite .. 58.43 ..
1.58.d:
अशीलिन्योऽव्रताश्चापि स्त्रियो मद्यामिषप्रियाः।
मायामात्रा भविष्यन्ति युगान्ते प्रत्युपस्थिते ॥ 58.43 ॥
1.58.m: Unchaste, without vows, fond of wine and meat, / women will be full of deceit when the end of the yuga is at hand.

1.58.s:
śvāpadaprabalatvañca gavāñcaivāpyupakṣayaḥ.
sādhūnāṃ vinivṛttiśca vidyāttasmin kalau yuge .. 58.44 ..
1.58.d:
श्वापदप्रबलत्वञ्च गवाञ्चैवाप्युपक्षयः।
साधूनां विनिवृत्तिश्च विद्यात्तस्मिन् कलौ युगे ॥ 58.44 ॥
1.58.m: One should know that in that Kali yuga beasts of prey will become strong, / cattle will decline, and virtuous men will disappear.

1.58.s:
tadā sūkṣme mahodarko durlabho bhogināṃ tathā.
caturāśramaśaithilyāddharmaḥ pravicaliṣyati .. 58.45 ..
1.58.d:
तदा सूक्ष्मे महोदर्को दुर्लभो भोगिनां तथा।
चतुराश्रमशैथिल्याद्धर्मः प्रविचलिष्यति ॥ 58.45 ॥
1.58.m: Then, though subtle [in performance], dharma has a great fruit, yet is hard for the worldly to attain; / from the laxity of the four stages of life, dharma will waver.

1.58.s:
tadā hyalpaphalā devī bhavedbhūmirmahīyasī.
śūdrāstapaścariṣyanti yugānte pratyupaśthite .. 58.46 ..
1.58.d:
तदा ह्यल्पफला देवी भवेद्भूमिर्महीयसी।
शूद्रास्तपश्चरिष्यन्ति युगान्ते प्रत्युपश्थिते ॥ 58.46 ॥
1.58.m: Then the earth, though great, will be of little yield. / Śūdras will practice asceticism when the end of the yuga is at hand.

1.58.s:
tadā hyaikāhiko dharmo dvāpare yaśca māsikaḥ.
tretāyāṃ vatsarasthaśca ekāhādatiricyate .. 58.47 ..
1.58.d:
तदा ह्यैकाहिको धर्मो द्वापरे यश्च मासिकः।
त्रेतायां वत्सरस्थश्च एकाहादतिरिच्यते ॥ 58.47 ॥
1.58.m: Then the dharma performed in a single day exceeds that of a month in the Dvāpara, / and that which takes a year in the Tretā, by [being accomplished in] one day.

1.58.s:
arakṣitāro harttāro balibhāgasya pārthivāḥ.
yugānteṣu bhaviṣyanti svarakṣaṇaparāyaṇāḥ .. 58.48 ..
1.58.d:
अरक्षितारो हर्त्तारो बलिभागस्य पार्थिवाः।
युगान्तेषु भविष्यन्ति स्वरक्षणपरायणाः ॥ 58.48 ॥
1.58.m: Failing to protect, taking their share of tribute, / kings at the end of the yugas will be intent only on protecting themselves.

1.58.s:
akṣatriyāśca rājāno viśaḥ śūdropajīvinaḥ.
śūdrābhivādinaḥ sarve yugānte dvijasattamāḥ .. 58.49 ..
1.58.d:
अक्षत्रियाश्च राजानो विशः शूद्रोपजीविनः।
शूद्राभिवादिनः सर्वे युगान्ते द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 58.49 ॥
1.58.m: Kings will be non-kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas will live by the work of śūdras; / at the end of the yuga, all the best of the twice-born will pay homage to śūdras.

1.58.s:
patayaśca bhaviṣyanti bahavo'smin kalau yuge.
citravarṣī tadā devo yadā syāttu yugakṣayaḥ .. 58.50 ..
1.58.d:
पतयश्च भविष्यन्ति बहवोऽस्मिन् कलौ युगे।
चित्रवर्षी तदा देवो यदा स्यात्तु युगक्षयः ॥ 58.50 ॥
1.58.m: And there will be many masters in this Kali yuga; / when the end of the yuga arrives, the god will rain fitfully.

1.58.s:
sarve vāṇijakāścāpi bhaviṣyantyadhame yuge.
bhūyiṣṭhaṃ kūṭamānaiśca paṇyavikrītatejanaiḥ .. 58.51 ..
1.58.d:
सर्वे वाणिजकाश्चापि भविष्यन्त्यधमे युगे।
भूयिष्ठं कूटमानैश्च पण्यविक्रीततेजनैः ॥ 58.51 ॥
1.58.m: All will become traders in that lowest yuga, / mostly with false measures and selling goods with deceit.

1.58.s:
kuśīlacaryā pāṣaṇḍairvṛthārūpaiḥ samāvṛtam.
puruṣālpaṃ bahustrīkaṃ yugānte paryupasthite .. 58.52 ..
1.58.d:
कुशीलचर्या पाषण्डैर्वृथारूपैः समावृतम्।
पुरुषाल्पं बहुस्त्रीकं युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते ॥ 58.52 ॥
1.58.m: The conduct of good morals will be encompassed by hypocritical heretics in vain forms; / when the end of the yuga is at hand, men will be few and women many.

1.58.s:
bahuyācanako loko bhaviṣyati parasparam.
kravyādanaḥ krūravākyo nārjavo nānasūyakaḥ .. 58.53 ..
1.58.d:
बहुयाचनको लोको भविष्यति परस्परम्।
क्रव्यादनः क्रूरवाक्यो नार्जवो नानसूयकः ॥ 58.53 ॥
1.58.m: People will beg constantly from one another; / eating meat, speaking cruelly, neither straightforward nor free from malice.

1.58.s:
na kṛte pratikartā ca kṣīṇo loko bhaviṣyati.
aśaṅkā caiva patite tadyugāntasya lakṣaṇam .. 58.54 ..
1.58.d:
न कृते प्रतिकर्ता च क्षीणो लोको भविष्यति।
अशङ्का चैव पतिते तद्युगान्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 58.54 ॥
1.58.m: None will return a favor done, and the world will be diminished; / there will be no hesitation [in associating] with the fallen—this is the mark of the end of the yuga.

1.58.s:
naraśūnyā vasumatī śūnyā caiva bhaviṣyati.
maṇḍalāni bhavantyatra deśeṣu nagareṣu ca .. 58.55 ..
1.58.d:
नरशून्या वसुमती शून्या चैव भविष्यति।
मण्डलानि भवन्त्यत्र देशेषु नगरेषु च ॥ 58.55 ॥
1.58.m: The earth will become devoid of men and desolate; / there will be factions formed in countries and in cities.

1.58.s:
alpodakā cālpaphalā bhaviṣyati vasundharā.
goptāraścāpyagoptāraḥ prabhaviṣyantyaśāsanāḥ .. 58.56 ..
1.58.d:
अल्पोदका चाल्पफला भविष्यति वसुन्धरा।
गोप्तारश्चाप्यगोप्तारः प्रभविष्यन्त्यशासनाः ॥ 58.56 ॥
1.58.m: The earth will have little water and bear little fruit; / protectors will become non-protectors, ruling without law.

1.58.s:
harttāraḥ pararatnānāṃ paradārapradharṣakāḥ.
kāmātmāno durātmāno hyadharmāt sāhasapriyāḥ .. 58.57 ..
1.58.d:
हर्त्तारः पररत्नानां परदारप्रधर्षकाः।
कामात्मानो दुरात्मानो ह्यधर्मात् साहसप्रियाः ॥ 58.57 ॥
1.58.m: They will seize others' jewels and assault others' wives; / lustful, wicked-natured, out of unrighteousness they will be fond of violence.

1.58.s:
anaṣṭacetanāḥ puṃso muktakeśāstu cūlikāḥ.
ūnaṣoḍaśavarṣāśca prajāyante yugakṣaye .. 58.58 ..
1.58.d:
अनष्टचेतनाः पुंसो मुक्तकेशास्तु चूलिकाः।
ऊनषोडशवर्षाश्च प्रजायन्ते युगक्षये ॥ 58.58 ॥
1.58.m: Men will be bereft of sense, with disheveled hair and topknots; / and at the end of the yuga, they will reproduce before reaching sixteen years of age.

1.58.s:
śukladantā jitākṣāśca muṇḍāḥ kāṣāyavāsasaḥ.
śūdrā dharmañcariṣyanti yugānte paryupasthite .. 58.59 ..
1.58.d:
शुक्लदन्ता जिताक्षाश्च मुण्डाः काषायवाससः।
शूद्रा धर्मञ्चरिष्यन्ति युगान्ते पर्युपस्थिते ॥ 58.59 ॥
1.58.m: With white teeth, subdued senses, shaven heads, and ochre robes, / śūdras will practice dharma when the end of the yuga arrives.

1.58.s:
sasyacaurā bhaviṣyaṃti tathā cailābhimarśanāḥ.
caurāścaurasya harttāro hanturharttāra eva va .. 58.60 ..
1.58.d:
सस्यचौरा भविष्यंति तथा चैलाभिमर्शनाः।
चौराश्चौरस्य हर्त्तारो हन्तुर्हर्त्तार एव व ॥ 58.60 ॥
1.58.m: There will be thieves of grain, and likewise those who steal clothes; / thieves will rob thieves, and killers will kill killers.

1.58.s:
jñānakarmaṇyuparate loke niṣkriyatāṅgate .
kīṭamūṣikasarpāśca dharṣayiṣyanti mānavān .. 58.61 ..
1.58.d:
ज्ञानकर्मण्युपरते लोके निष्क्रियताङ्गते ।
कीटमूषिकसर्पाश्च धर्षयिष्यन्ति मानवान् ॥ 58.61 ॥
1.58.m: When knowledge and ritual actions cease and the world becomes inactive, / insects, mice, and serpents will torment human beings.

1.58.s:
subhikṣaṃ kṣemamārogyaṃ sāmarthyaṃ durlabhaṃ bhavet.
kauśikāḥ prativatsyanti deśān kṣudbhayapīḍitān .. 58.62 ..
1.58.d:
सुभिक्षं क्षेममारोग्यं सामर्थ्यं दुर्लभं भवेत्।
कौशिकाः प्रतिवत्स्यन्ति देशान् क्षुद्भयपीडितान् ॥ 58.62 ॥
1.58.m: Abundance of food, security, health, and capability will become hard to find; / owls will inhabit lands afflicted by hunger and fear.

1.58.s:
duḥkhenābhiplutānāñca paramāyuḥ śataṃ bhavet.
dṛśyante na ca dṛśyante vedāḥ kaliyuge'khilāḥ .. 58.63 ..
1.58.d:
दुःखेनाभिप्लुतानाञ्च परमायुः शतं भवेत्।
दृश्यन्ते न च दृश्यन्ते वेदाः कलियुगेऽखिलाः ॥ 58.63 ॥
1.58.m: For those overwhelmed by sorrow, the maximum lifespan will be a hundred years; / in the Kali yuga, the Vedas will be seen and not seen completely.

1.58.s:
utsīdanti tathā yajñāḥ kevalā dharmapīḍitāḥ.
kaṣāyiṇaśca nirgranthāstathā kāpālinaśca ha .. 58.64 ..
1.58.d:
उत्सीदन्ति तथा यज्ञाः केवला धर्मपीडिताः।
कषायिणश्च निर्ग्रन्थास्तथा कापालिनश्च ह ॥ 58.64 ॥
1.58.m: Sacrifices, completely ruined, will thus decay; / and there will be wearers of ochre robes, Nirgranthas, and Kāpālikas,

1.58.s:
vedavikrayiṇaścānye tīrthavikrayiṇo'pare .
varṇāśramāṇāṃ ye cānye pāṣaṇḍāḥ paripanthinaḥ .. 58.65 ..
1.58.d:
वेदविक्रयिणश्चान्ये तीर्थविक्रयिणोऽपरे ।
वर्णाश्रमाणां ये चान्ये पाषण्डाः परिपन्थिनः ॥ 58.65 ॥
1.58.m: others who sell the Vedas, and others who sell holy bathing-places, / and other heretics who are obstacles to the social classes and stages of life.

1.58.s:
utpadyante tathā te vai saṃprāpte tu kalau yuge.
nādhīyante tadā vedāḥ śūdrā dharmārthakovidāḥ .. 58.66 ..
1.58.d:
उत्पद्यन्ते तथा ते वै संप्राप्ते तु कलौ युगे।
नाधीयन्ते तदा वेदाः शूद्रा धर्मार्थकोविदाः ॥ 58.66 ॥
1.58.m: They will indeed arise when the Kali yuga arrives; / the Vedas will not be studied then, while śūdras will become skilled in dharma and worldly affairs.

1.58.s:
yajante nāśvamedhena rājānaḥ śūdrayonayaḥ.
strīvadhaṃ govadhaṃ kṛtvā hatvā caiva parasparam.
upahanyustadānyonyaṃ sādhayanti tathā prajāḥ .. 58.67 ..
1.58.d:
यजन्ते नाश्वमेधेन राजानः शूद्रयोनयः।
स्त्रीवधं गोवधं कृत्वा हत्वा चैव परस्परम्।
उपहन्युस्तदान्योन्यं साधयन्ति तथा प्रजाः ॥ 58.67 ॥
1.58.m: Kings born of śūdra wombs will not sacrifice with the horse sacrifice; / slaying women and cows, and slaying one another, / they will strike each other down then, and so subdue the subjects.

1.58.s:
duḥkhapracārato'lpāyurdeśotsādaḥ sarogatā.
moho glānistathāsaukhyaṃ tamovṛttaṃ kalau smṛtam .. 58.68 ..
1.58.d:
दुःखप्रचारतोऽल्पायुर्देशोत्सादः सरोगता।
मोहो ग्लानिस्तथासौख्यं तमोवृत्तं कलौ स्मृतम् ॥ 58.68 ॥
1.58.m: From the spread of suffering comes short life, ruin of the country, disease, / delusion, dejection, and distress—this is remembered as the way of darkness in Kali.

1.58.s:
prajā tu bhrūṇahatyāyāmatha vai sampravarttate.
tasmādāyurbalaṃ rūpaṃ kaliṃ prāpya prahīyate.
duḥkhenābhiplutānāṃ vai paramāyuḥ śataṃ nṛṇām .. 58.69 ..
1.58.d:
प्रजा तु भ्रूणहत्यायामथ वै सम्प्रवर्त्तते।
तस्मादायुर्बलं रूपं कलिं प्राप्य प्रहीयते।
दुःखेनाभिप्लुतानां वै परमायुः शतं नृणाम् ॥ 58.69 ॥
1.58.m: People indeed proceed to the slaying of embryos; / therefore, reaching Kali, life, strength, and beauty decay; / for men overwhelmed by sorrow, the maximum lifespan will be a hundred years.

1.58.s:
dṛśyante nābhidṛśyante vedāḥ kaliyuge'khilāḥ.
utsīdante tadā yajñāḥ kovalā dharmapīḍitāḥ .. 58.70 ..
1.58.d:
दृश्यन्ते नाभिदृश्यन्ते वेदाः कलियुगेऽखिलाः।
उत्सीदन्ते तदा यज्ञाः कोवला धर्मपीडिताः ॥ 58.70 ॥
1.58.m: In the Kali yuga, all the Vedas are seen and not seen; / sacrifices then decay completely, afflicted by unrighteousness.

1.58.s:
tadā tvalpena kālena siddhiṃ yāsyanti mānavāḥ.
dhanyā dharmañcariṣyanti yugānte dvijasattamāḥ .. 58.71 ..
1.58.d:
तदा त्वल्पेन कालेन सिद्धिं यास्यन्ति मानवाः।
धन्या धर्मञ्चरिष्यन्ति युगान्ते द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 58.71 ॥
1.58.m: Then, however, human beings will attain perfection in a short time; / blessed are the best of the twice-born who will practice dharma at the end of the yuga.

1.58.s:
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmaṃ ye carantyanasūyakāḥ.
tretāyāṃ vārṣiko dharmo dvāpare māsikaḥ smṛtaḥ.
yathāśaktiṃ caran prājñastadahnā prāpruyāt kalau .. 58.72 ..
1.58.d:
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितं धर्मं ये चरन्त्यनसूयकाः।
त्रेतायां वार्षिको धर्मो द्वापरे मासिकः स्मृतः।
यथाशक्तिं चरन् प्राज्ञस्तदह्ना प्राप्रुयात् कलौ ॥ 58.72 ॥
1.58.m: Those who, free from malice, practice the dharma declared by the Śruti and Smṛti— / the dharma that in Tretā took a year, in Dvāpara is remembered as taking a month; / practicing according to his ability, a wise man can attain that in a single day in Kali.

1.58.s:
eṣā kaliyuge'vasthā sandhyāṃśantu nibodha me .
yuge yuge tu hīyante trīṃstrīn pādāṃśca siddhayaḥ .. 58.73 ..
1.58.d:
एषा कलियुगेऽवस्था सन्ध्यांशन्तु निबोध मे ।
युगे युगे तु हीयन्ते त्रींस्त्रीन् पादांश्च सिद्धयः ॥ 58.73 ॥
1.58.m: This is the condition in the Kali yuga; now hear from me regarding its twilight portion: / in each yuga, the perfections decline by three quarters.

1.58.s:
yugasvabhāvātsandhyāstu tiṣṭhantīmāstu pādaśaḥ.
sandhyāsvabhāvāccāṃśeṣu pādaśaste pratiṣṭhitāḥ .. 58.74 ..
1.58.d:
युगस्वभावात्सन्ध्यास्तु तिष्ठन्तीमास्तु पादशः।
सन्ध्यास्वभावाच्चांशेषु पादशस्ते प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥ 58.74 ॥
1.58.m: By the nature of the yuga, these twilights stand quarter by quarter; / and by the nature of the twilight, they are established in quarters within its parts.

1.58.s:
evaṃ sandhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike.
teṣāṃ śāstā hyasādhūnāṃ bhṛgūṇāṃ nidhanotthitaḥ .. 58.75 ..
1.58.d:
एवं सन्ध्यांशके काले सम्प्राप्ते तु युगान्तिके।
तेषां शास्ता ह्यसाधूनां भृगूणां निधनोत्थितः ॥ 58.75 ॥
1.58.m: When the twilight portion has thus arrived near the end of the yuga, / a punisher of those wicked people will arise from the lineage of the Bhṛgus.

1.58.s:
gotreṇa vai candramaso nāmnā pramitirucyate.
mādhavasya tu soṃśena pūrvaṃ svāyambhuve'ntare .. 58.76 ..
1.58.d:
गोत्रेण वै चन्द्रमसो नाम्ना प्रमितिरुच्यते।
माधवस्य तु सोंशेन पूर्वं स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे ॥ 58.76 ॥
1.58.m: By family lineage he belongs to the Moon; by name he is called Pramiti; / formerly, in the Svāyambhuva manvantara, he was an portion of Mādhava.

1.58.s:
samāḥ sa viṃśatiṃ pūrṇāḥ paryaṭan vai vasundharām.
ācakarṣa sa vai senāṃ savājirathakuñjarām .. 58.77 ..
1.58.d:
समाः स विंशतिं पूर्णाः पर्यटन् वै वसुन्धराम्।
आचकर्ष स वै सेनां सवाजिरथकुञ्जराम् ॥ 58.77 ॥
1.58.m: Wandering over the earth for twenty full years, / he gathered an army with horses, chariots, and elephants,

1.58.s:
pragṛhītāyudhairvipraiḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ.
sa tadā taiḥ parivṛto mlecchān hanti sahasraśaḥ .. 58.78 ..
1.58.d:
प्रगृहीतायुधैर्विप्रैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः।
स तदा तैः परिवृतो म्लेच्छान् हन्ति सहस्रशः ॥ 58.78 ॥
1.58.m: with brāhmaṇas holding weapons by hundreds and thousands; / surrounded then by them, he slays mlecchas by thousands.

1.58.s:
sa hatvā sarvagaścaiva rājñastān śūdrayonijāt.
pāṣaṇḍān sa tataḥ sarvānniḥśeṣān kṛtavān prabhuḥ .. 58.79 ..
1.58.d:
स हत्वा सर्वगश्चैव राज्ञस्तान् शूद्रयोनिजात्।
पाषण्डान् स ततः सर्वान्निःशेषान् कृतवान् प्रभुः ॥ 58.79 ॥
1.58.m: Going everywhere, he slew those kings born of śūdra wombs; / then that lord completely annihilated all the heretics.

1.58.s:
nātyarthaṃ dhārmikā ye ca tān sarvān hanti sarvaśaḥ.
varṇavyatyāsajātāṃśca ye ca tānupajīvinaḥ .. 58.80 ..
1.58.d:
नात्यर्थं धार्मिका ये च तान् सर्वान् हन्ति सर्वशः।
वर्णव्यत्यासजातांश्च ये च तानुपजीविनः ॥ 58.80 ॥
1.58.m: Those who are not exceedingly righteous—he slays all of them everywhere, / as well as those born of the confusion of social classes and those who live by them:

1.58.s:
udīcyānmadhyadeśāṃśca pārvatīyāṃstathaiva ca.
prācyān pratīcyāṃśca tathā vindhyapṛṣṭhāparāntikān .. 58.81 ..
1.58.d:
उदीच्यान्मध्यदेशांश्च पार्वतीयांस्तथैव च।
प्राच्यान् प्रतीच्यांश्च तथा विन्ध्यपृष्ठापरान्तिकान् ॥ 58.81 ॥
1.58.m: northerners, inhabitants of the central land, and mountaineers likewise; / easterners, westerners, and the western peoples on the ridge of the Vindhya;

1.58.s:
tathaiva dākṣiṇātyāṃśca draviḍān siṃhalaiḥ saha.
gāndārān pāradāṃścaiva pahnavān yavanāṃstathā .. 58.82 ..
1.58.d:
तथैव दाक्षिणात्यांश्च द्रविडान् सिंहलैः सह।
गान्दारान् पारदांश्चैव पह्नवान् यवनांस्तथा ॥ 58.82 ॥
1.58.m: likewise southerners, Draviḍas along with Siṃhalas, / Gāndhāras and Pāradas, Pahlavas and Yavanas,

1.58.s:
tuṣārān varvarāṃścīnān śūlikān daradān khasān.
lampākāntha ketāṃśca kirātānāñca jātayaḥ .. 58.83 ..
1.58.d:
तुषारान् वर्वरांश्चीनान् शूलिकान् दरदान् खसान्।
लम्पाकान्थ केतांश्च किरातानाञ्च जातयः ॥ 58.83 ॥
1.58.m: Tuṣāras, Barbaras, Cīnas, Śūlikas, Daradas, Khasas, / Lampākas, then Ketas, and the tribes of the Kirātas.

1.58.s:
pravṛttacakro balavān mlecchānāmantakṛdvibhuḥ.
adhṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ cacārātha vasundharām .. 58.84 ..
1.58.d:
प्रवृत्तचक्रो बलवान् म्लेच्छानामन्तकृद्विभुः।
अधृष्यः सर्वभूतानां चचाराथ वसुन्धराम् ॥ 58.84 ॥
1.58.m: With rolling wheel, powerful, making an end of the mlecchas, the lord, / invincible to all beings, then traversed the earth.

1.58.s:
mādhavasya tu soṃśena devasya hi vijajñivān .
pūrvajanmavidhijñaiśca pramitirnāma vīryavān .. 58.85 ..
1.58.d:
माधवस्य तु सोंशेन देवस्य हि विजज्ञिवान् ।
पूर्वजन्मविधिज्ञैश्च प्रमितिर्नाम वीर्यवान् ॥ 58.85 ॥
1.58.m: For that powerful one, born as a portion of the god Mādhava, / is known by those knowing the rules of previous births by the name Pramiti.

1.58.s:
gotreṇa vai candramasaḥ pūrve kaliyuge prabhuḥ.
dvātriṃśe'bhyudite varṣe prakrānte viṃśatiṃ samāḥ .. 58.86 ..
1.58.d:
गोत्रेण वै चन्द्रमसः पूर्वे कलियुगे प्रभुः।
द्वात्रिंशेऽभ्युदिते वर्षे प्रक्रान्ते विंशतिं समाः ॥ 58.86 ॥
1.58.m: By lineage of the Moon, a lord in the former Kali yuga, / having arisen in his thirty-second year, he campaigned for twenty years,

1.58.s:
vinighnan sarvabhūtāni mānavāni sahasraśaḥ.
kṛtvā vīryāvaśeṣāntu pṛthvīṃ ṟūḍhena karmaṇā .
parasparanimittena kopenākasmikena tu .. 58.87 ..
1.58.d:
विनिघ्नन् सर्वभूतानि मानवानि सहस्रशः।
कृत्वा वीर्यावशेषान्तु पृथ्वीं ṟऊढेन कर्मणा ।
परस्परनिमित्तेन कोपेनाकस्मिकेन तु ॥ 58.87 ॥
1.58.m: slaying human beings and all living things by thousands; / leaving only vigor remaining on the earth by his harsh action, / through mutual conflict and sudden wrath.

1.58.s:
sa sādhayitvā vṛṣalān prāyaśastānadhārmikān .
gaṅgāyamunayormadhye niṣṭhāṃ prāptaḥ sahānugaḥ .. 58.88 ..
1.58.d:
स साधयित्वा वृषलान् प्रायशस्तानधार्मिकान् ।
गङ्गायमुनयोर्मध्ये निष्ठां प्राप्तः सहानुगः ॥ 58.88 ॥
1.58.m: Having subdued those śūdras, who were mostly unrighteous, / between the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā he reached his end, together with his followers.

1.58.s:
tato vyatīte tasmiṃstu amātye satyasainike.
utsādya pārthivān sarvān mlecchāṃścaiva sahasraśaḥ .. 58.89 ..
1.58.d:
ततो व्यतीते तस्मिंस्तु अमात्ये सत्यसैनिके।
उत्साद्य पार्थिवान् सर्वान् म्लेच्छांश्चैव सहस्रशः ॥ 58.89 ॥
1.58.m: Then, when he had passed away, together with his minister whose troops were faithful, / after he had overthrown all the earthly kings and mlecchas by thousands,

1.58.s:
tatra sandhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike.
sthitāsvalpāvaśiṣṭāsu prajāsviha vkacit vkacit .. 58.90 ..
1.58.d:
तत्र सन्ध्यांशके काले सम्प्राप्ते तु युगान्तिके।
स्थितास्वल्पावशिष्टासु प्रजास्विह व्कचित् व्कचित् ॥ 58.90 ॥
1.58.m: at that twilight portion, when the close of the yuga had arrived, / with the remaining population left very small and scattered here and there,

1.58.s:
apragrahāstatastā vai lokaceṣṭāstu vṛndaśaḥ.
upahiṃsanti cānyonyaṃ prapadyante parasparam .. 58.91 ..
1.58.d:
अप्रग्रहास्ततस्ता वै लोकचेष्टास्तु वृन्दशः।
उपहिंसन्ति चान्योन्यं प्रपद्यन्ते परस्परम् ॥ 58.91 ॥
1.58.m: Then, unrestrained, those earthly activities [proceeded] in crowds; / they injured one another and preyed on each other.

1.58.s:
arājake yugavaśāt saṃśaye samupasthite.
prajāstā vai tataḥ sarvāḥ parasparabhayārditāḥ .. 58.92 ..
1.58.d:
अराजके युगवशात् संशये समुपस्थिते।
प्रजास्ता वै ततः सर्वाः परस्परभयार्दिताः ॥ 58.92 ॥
1.58.m: When anarchy arose due to the influence of the yuga and uncertainty set in, / all those creatures, tormented by mutual fear,

1.58.s:
vyākulāśca pariśrāntāstyaktvā dārān gṛhāṇi ca.
svān prāṇān samavekṣanto niṣṭhāṃ prāptāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ .. 58.93 ..
1.58.d:
व्याकुलाश्च परिश्रान्तास्त्यक्त्वा दारान् गृहाणि च।
स्वान् प्राणान् समवेक्षन्तो निष्ठां प्राप्ताः सुदुःखिताः ॥ 58.93 ॥
1.58.m: Confused and exhausted, abandoning their wives and homes, / caring only for their own lives, reached their end in extreme sorrow.

1.58.s:
naṣṭe śraute smṛte dharme parasparahatāstadā.
nirmaryādā nirākrandā niḥsnehā nirapatrapāḥ .. 58.94 ..
1.58.d:
नष्टे श्रौते स्मृते धर्मे परस्परहतास्तदा।
निर्मर्यादा निराक्रन्दा निःस्नेहा निरपत्रपाः ॥ 58.94 ॥
1.58.m: When the dharma taught by Śruti and Smṛti was destroyed, they were then slain by one another, / lawless, without refuge, devoid of affection, and shameless.

1.58.s:
naṣṭe varpe pratihatā hrasvakāḥ pañjaviṃśakāḥ.
hitvā dārāṃśca putrāṃśca viṣādavyākulendriyāḥ .. 58.95 ..
1.58.d:
नष्टे वर्पे प्रतिहता ह्रस्वकाः पञ्जविंशकाः।
हित्वा दारांश्च पुत्रांश्च विषादव्याकुलेन्द्रियाः ॥ 58.95 ॥
1.58.m: Stunted, twenty-five [years old], thwarted when their appearance was ruined, / leaving their wives and sons, their senses bewildered by despair,

1.58.s:
anāvṛṣṭihatāścaiva vārttāmutsṛjya duḥkhitāḥ.
pratyantāṃstānnipevante hitvā janapadān svakān .. 58.96 ..
1.58.d:
अनावृष्टिहताश्चैव वार्त्तामुत्सृज्य दुःखिताः।
प्रत्यन्तांस्तान्निपेवन्ते हित्वा जनपदान् स्वकान् ॥ 58.96 ॥
1.58.m: Stricken by drought, abandoning their livelihoods, afflicted with grief, / they took refuge in the borderlands, leaving their own countries.

1.58.s:
saritaḥ sāgarān kūpān sevante parvatāṃstadā.
madhumāṃsairmūlaphalairvarttayanti suduḥkhitāḥ .. 58.97 ..
1.58.d:
सरितः सागरान् कूपान् सेवन्ते पर्वतांस्तदा।
मधुमांसैर्मूलफलैर्वर्त्तयन्ति सुदुःखिताः ॥ 58.97 ॥
1.58.m: Then they resorted to rivers, oceans, wells, and mountains; / deeply distressed, they subsisted on honey, meat, roots, and fruits.

1.58.s:
cīravastrājinadharā niṣpatrā niṣparigrahāḥ.
varṇāśramaparibhraṣṭāḥ saṅkaraṃ ghoramāsthitāḥ .. 58.98 ..
1.58.d:
चीरवस्त्राजिनधरा निष्पत्रा निष्परिग्रहाः।
वर्णाश्रमपरिभ्रष्टाः सङ्करं घोरमास्थिताः ॥ 58.98 ॥
1.58.m: Wearing rags, bark, and animal skins, without property, without possessions, / fallen from class and stage of life, they fell into terrible mixture.

1.58.s:
etāḥ kāṣṭhāmanuprāptā alpaśeṣāstathā prajāḥ .
jarāvyādhikṣudhāviṣṭā duḥkhānnirvedamāgaman .. 58.99 ..
1.58.d:
एताः काष्ठामनुप्राप्ता अल्पशेषास्तथा प्रजाः ।
जराव्याधिक्षुधाविष्टा दुःखान्निर्वेदमागमन् ॥ 58.99 ॥
1.58.m: Thus the few remaining creatures reached an extreme limit; / beset by old age, disease, and hunger, they attained revulsion through suffering.

1.58.s:
vicāraṇantu nirvedāt sāmyāvasthā vicāraṇāt.
sāmyāvasthāsu sambodhaḥ sambodhāddharmaśīlatā .. 58.100 ..
1.58.d:
विचारणन्तु निर्वेदात् साम्यावस्था विचारणात्।
साम्यावस्थासु सम्बोधः सम्बोधाद्धर्मशीलता ॥ 58.100 ॥
1.58.m: From revulsion comes reflection, and from reflection a state of equanimity; / in states of equanimity arises awakening, and from awakening comes righteousness.

1.58.s:
tāsupagamayuktāsu kaliśiṣṭāsu vai svayam.
ahorātraṃ tadā tāsāṃ yugantu parivarttate .. 58.101 ..
1.58.d:
तासुपगमयुक्तासु कलिशिष्टासु वै स्वयम्।
अहोरात्रं तदा तासां युगन्तु परिवर्त्तते ॥ 58.101 ॥
1.58.m: When those [creatures] remaining from the Kali [yuga] had naturally attained this, / the yuga then turned for them like day and night.

1.58.s:
cittasammohanaṃ kṛtvā tāsāntaiḥ saptamantu tat.
bhāvino'rthasya ca balāttataḥ kṛtamavartata .. 58.102 ..
1.58.d:
चित्तसम्मोहनं कृत्वा तासान्तैः सप्तमन्तु तत्।
भाविनोऽर्थस्य च बलात्ततः कृतमवर्तत ॥ 58.102 ॥
1.58.m: When the seventh [period] that caused their minds to be bewildered was [ended] by those [means], / then, by the force of what was destined to be, the Kṛta [yuga] commenced.

1.58.s:
pravṛtte tu punastasmiṃstataḥ kṛtayuge tu vai.
utpannāḥ kaliśiṣṭāstu kārtayugyaḥ prajāmtadā .. 58.103 ..
1.58.d:
प्रवृत्ते तु पुनस्तस्मिंस्ततः कृतयुगे तु वै।
उत्पन्नाः कलिशिष्टास्तु कार्तयुग्यः प्रजाम्तदा ॥ 58.103 ॥
1.58.m: When that Kṛta yuga commenced once again, / the creatures remaining from Kali then became subjects of the Kṛta yuga.

1.58.s:
tiṣṭhanti ceha ye siddhāḥ sudṛṣṭā vicaranti ca.
sadā saptarṣayaścaiva tatra te ca vyavasthitāḥ .. 58.104 ..
1.58.d:
तिष्ठन्ति चेह ये सिद्धाः सुदृष्टा विचरन्ति च।
सदा सप्तर्षयश्चैव तत्र ते च व्यवस्थिताः ॥ 58.104 ॥
1.58.m: The siddhas who abide here, clearly seen and wandering about, / and the seven seers always remain stationed there.

1.58.s:
brahmakṣatraviśaḥ śūdrā bījārthaṃ ye smṛtā iha.
kalijaiḥ saha te sarve nirviśeṣāstadābhavan .. 58.105 ..
1.58.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशः शूद्रा बीजार्थं ये स्मृता इह।
कलिजैः सह ते सर्वे निर्विशेषास्तदाभवन् ॥ 58.105 ॥
1.58.m: Those who are handed down here as seeds—brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras— / then all became indistinguishable along with those born of Kali.

1.58.s:
teṣāṃ saptarṣayo dharma kathayantītareṣu ca .
varṇā śramācārayuktaḥ śrautaḥ smārto dvidhā tu saḥ .. 58.106 ..
1.58.d:
तेषां सप्तर्षयो धर्म कथयन्तीतरेषु च ।
वर्णा श्रमाचारयुक्तः श्रौतः स्मार्तो द्विधा तु सः ॥ 58.106 ॥
1.58.m: The seven seers declared dharma to them and to the others— / that which is endowed with the conduct of classes and stages of life, twofold as Śruti and Smṛti.

1.58.s:
tatasteṣu kriyāvatsu varttante vai prajāḥ kṛte .
śrautaḥ smārttaḥ kṛtānāntu dharmaḥ saptarṣidarśitaḥ .. 58.107 ..
1.58.d:
ततस्तेषु क्रियावत्सु वर्त्तन्ते वै प्रजाः कृते ।
श्रौतः स्मार्त्तः कृतानान्तु धर्मः सप्तर्षिदर्शितः ॥ 58.107 ॥
1.58.m: Then, as those [seers] performed rites, the creatures lived in the Kṛta [yuga]; / the dharma shown by the seven seers to those of the Kṛta [age] is rooted in Śruti and Smṛti.

1.58.s:
tāsu dharmavyavastārthaṃ tiṣṭhantīhāyugakṣayāt .
manvantarādhikāreṣu tiṣṭhanti munayastu vai .. 58.108 ..
1.58.d:
तासु धर्मव्यवस्तार्थं तिष्ठन्तीहायुगक्षयात् ।
मन्वन्तराधिकारेषु तिष्ठन्ति मुनयस्तु वै ॥ 58.108 ॥
1.58.m: The sages remain here until the end of the yuga to establish dharma among them; / indeed, they remain in their offices throughout the cosmic ages of Manus.

1.58.s:
yathā dāvapradagdheṣu tṛṇeṣviha tape ṛtau .
navānāṃ prathamaṃ dṛṣṭasteṣāṃ mūle tu sambhavaḥ .. 58.109 ..
1.58.d:
यथा दावप्रदग्धेषु तृणेष्विह तपे ऋतौ ।
नवानां प्रथमं दृष्टस्तेषां मूले तु सम्भवः ॥ 58.109 ॥
1.58.m: Just as here, in the hot season, when grasses are burnt by a forest fire, / the growth of new [shoots] is seen first at their roots,

1.58.s:
evaṃ yugādyugasteha santānastu parasparam .
varttate hyavyavacchedādyāvanmanvantarakṣayaḥ .. 58.110 ..
1.58.d:
एवं युगाद्युगस्तेह सन्तानस्तु परस्परम् ।
वर्त्तते ह्यव्यवच्छेदाद्यावन्मन्वन्तरक्षयः ॥ 58.110 ॥
1.58.m: In this way the succession of yugas proceeds here uninterruptedly / from one to the next until the end of the cosmic age of a Manu.

1.58.s:
sukhamāyurbalaṃ rūpaṃ dharmārthau kāma eva ca .
yugeṣvetāni hīyante trīṇi pādakrameṇa tu .. 58.111 ..
1.58.d:
सुखमायुर्बलं रूपं धर्मार्थौ काम एव च ।
युगेष्वेतानि हीयन्ते त्रीणि पादक्रमेण तु ॥ 58.111 ॥
1.58.m: Happiness, lifespan, strength, beauty, dharma, wealth, and desire— / these three diminish in the yugas by quarter-measures in succession.

1.58.s:
sasandhyaṃśeṣu hīyante yugānāṃ dharmasiddhayaḥ.
ityeṣa pratisandhirvaḥ kīrttitastu mayā dvijāḥ .. 58.112 ..
1.58.d:
ससन्ध्यंशेषु हीयन्ते युगानां धर्मसिद्धयः।
इत्येष प्रतिसन्धिर्वः कीर्त्तितस्तु मया द्विजाः ॥ 58.112 ॥
1.58.m: Together with their twilights and twilight portions, the achievements of dharma of the yugas diminish. / Thus this transition has been declared to you by me, O twice-born!

1.58.s: caturyugānāṃ sarveṣāmetenaiva prasādhanam ..
1.58.d: चतुर्युगानां सर्वेषामेतेनैव प्रसाधनम् ॥
1.58.m:
The accomplishment of all the four yugas is through this alone;
this recurrence of the four yugas proceeds up to a thousand [cycles].

1.58.s: eṣā caturyugāvṛttirāsahasrāt pravarttate .. 58.113 ..
1.58.d: एषा चतुर्युगावृत्तिरासहस्रात् प्रवर्त्तते ॥ 58.113 ॥

1.58.s:
brahmaṇastadahaḥ proktaṃ rātriśca tāvatī smṛtā .
atrārjavaṃ jaḍībhāvo bhūtānāmāyugakṣayāt .. 58.114 ..
1.58.d:
ब्रह्मणस्तदहः प्रोक्तं रात्रिश्च तावती स्मृता ।
अत्रार्जवं जडीभावो भूतानामायुगक्षयात् ॥ 58.114 ॥
1.58.m: That is declared to be a day of Brahmā, and his night is handed down as of equal length. / In this cycle, straightness and torpor occur for beings until the end of the yuga.

1.58.s:
etadeva tu sarveṣāṃ yugānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam.
eṣā caturyugānāntu gaṇanā hyekasaptatiḥ.
krameṇa parivṛttā tu manorantaramucyate .. 58.115 ..
1.58.d:
एतदेव तु सर्वेषां युगानां लक्षणं स्मृतम्।
एषा चतुर्युगानान्तु गणना ह्येकसप्ततिः।
क्रमेण परिवृत्ता तु मनोरन्तरमुच्यते ॥ 58.115 ॥
1.58.m: This alone is handed down as the characteristic of all the yugas; / and seventy-one of these four yugas, / revolving in order, is called the cosmic age of a Manu.

1.58.s:
caturyuge tathaikasmin bhavatīha yathāśrutam.
tathā cānyeṣu bhavati punastadvai yathākramam .. 58.116 ..
1.58.d:
चतुर्युगे तथैकस्मिन् भवतीह यथाश्रुतम्।
तथा चान्येषु भवति पुनस्तद्वै यथाक्रमम् ॥ 58.116 ॥
1.58.m: As has been heard, so it occurs in one [cycle of] four yugas here; / and so it occurs again in the others, in regular order.

1.58.s:
sarge sarge yathā bhedā utpadyante tathaiva tu .
pañcaviṃśatparimitā na nyūnā nādhikāstathā .. 58.117 ..
1.58.d:
सर्गे सर्गे यथा भेदा उत्पद्यन्ते तथैव तु ।
पञ्चविंशत्परिमिता न न्यूना नाधिकास्तथा ॥ 58.117 ॥
1.58.m: Just as distinctions arise in creation after creation, in that very manner / they are measured as twenty-five, neither fewer nor more.

1.58.s:
tathā kalpayugaiḥ sārddhaṃ bhavanti samalakṣaṇāḥ.
manvantarāṇāṃ sarveṣāmetadeva tu lakṣaṇam .. 58.118 ..
1.58.d:
तथा कल्पयुगैः सार्द्धं भवन्ति समलक्षणाः।
मन्वन्तराणां सर्वेषामेतदेव तु लक्षणम् ॥ 58.118 ॥
1.58.m: Thus they are of identical characteristics throughout the yugas of the aeons; / this alone is the characteristic of all the cosmic ages of Manus.

1.58.s:
tathā yugānāṃ parivarttanāni cirapravṛttāni yugasvabhavāt .
tathā na santiṣṭhati jīvalokaḥ kṣayodayābhyāṃ parivarttamānaḥ .. 58.119 ..
1.58.d:
तथा युगानां परिवर्त्तनानि चिरप्रवृत्तानि युगस्वभवात् ।
तथा न सन्तिष्ठति जीवलोकः क्षयोदयाभ्यां परिवर्त्तमानः ॥ 58.119 ॥
1.58.m: Thus the revolutions of the yugas proceed for a long time by the inherent nature of the yugas; / so the world of living beings does not remain fixed, revolving through decline and rise.

1.58.s:
ityetallakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ yugānāṃ vai samāsataḥ.
atītānāgatānāṃ vai sarvāṇyevāntarāṇi .. 58.120 ..
1.58.d:
इत्येतल्लक्षणं प्रोक्तं युगानां वै समासतः।
अतीतानागतानां वै सर्वाण्येवान्तराणि ॥ 58.120 ॥
1.58.m: Thus this characteristic of the yugas has been declared in brief; / indeed, all the intervals, past and future, [are like this].

1.58.s:
anāgateṣu tadvacca tarkkaḥ kāryo vijānatā.
manvantareṣu sarveṣu atītānāgateṣviha .. 58.121 ..
1.58.d:
अनागतेषु तद्वच्च तर्क्कः कार्यो विजानता।
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु अतीतानागतेष्विह ॥ 58.121 ॥
1.58.m: In the same way, the wise person should infer about future ones, / across all the cosmic ages of Manus here, both past and future.

1.58.s:
manvantareṇa caikena sarvāṇyevāntarāṇi vai.
vyākhyātāni vijānīdvaṃ kalpe kalpena caiva hi .. 58.122 ..
1.58.d:
मन्वन्तरेण चैकेन सर्वाण्येवान्तराणि वै।
व्याख्यातानि विजानीद्वं कल्पे कल्पेन चैव हि ॥ 58.122 ॥
1.58.m: Know that through one cosmic age of a Manu, all the intervals are explained, / and through one aeon, each aeon [is explained].

1.58.s:
asyābhimāninaḥ sarve nāmarūpairbhavantyuta.
devā hyaṣṭavidhā ye ca iha manvantareśvarāḥ .. 58.123 ..
1.58.d:
अस्याभिमानिनः सर्वे नामरूपैर्भवन्त्युत।
देवा ह्यष्टविधा ये च इह मन्वन्तरेश्वराः ॥ 58.123 ॥
1.58.m: All the deities presiding over this exist through names and forms, / and the eight classes of gods who are the lords of the cosmic age of a Manu here,

1.58.s:
ṛṣayo manavaścaiva sarve tulyāḥ prayojanaiḥ.
evaṃ varṇāśramāṇāntu pravibhāgo yuge yuge .. 58.124 ..
1.58.d:
ऋषयो मनवश्चैव सर्वे तुल्याः प्रयोजनैः।
एवं वर्णाश्रमाणान्तु प्रविभागो युगे युगे ॥ 58.124 ॥
1.58.m: The seers and the Manus—all have identical functions. / Thus the division of the classes and stages of life occurs in yuga after yuga.

1.58.s:
yugasvabhāvācca tathā vidhatte vai sadā prabhuḥ .
varṇāśramavibhāgaśca yugāni yugasiddhaye .. 58.125 ..
1.58.d:
युगस्वभावाच्च तथा विधत्ते वै सदा प्रभुः ।
वर्णाश्रमविभागश्च युगानि युगसिद्धये ॥ 58.125 ॥
1.58.m: And thus, according to the nature of the yuga, the Lord always establishes / the division of classes and stages of life, and the yugas for the achievement of the yuga['s purpose].

1.58.s:
anuṣaṅgaḥ samākhyātaḥ sṛṣṭisargannibodhata.
vistareṇānupūrvyā ca sthitiṃ vakṣye yugeṣviha .. 58.126 ..
1.58.d:
अनुषङ्गः समाख्यातः सृष्टिसर्गन्निबोधत।
विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या च स्थितिं वक्ष्ये युगेष्विह ॥ 58.126 ॥
1.58.m: The incidental connection has been fully declared; learn now of the process of creation. / I shall explain in detail and in proper order the order of things in the yugas here.

1.58.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte caturyugākhyānaṃ nāmāṣṭapañcāśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 58 ..
1.58.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते चतुर्युगाख्यानं नामाष्टपञ्चाशोऽध्यायः ॥ 58 ॥
1.58.m: Thus ends the fifty-eighth chapter, named 'Account of the Four Yugas', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa proclaimed by Vāyu.

1.59.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.59.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.59.m:
The Sūta said:
Listen indeed to the creatures that are born in the yugas:
asuric, serpentine, bovine, avian, ghostly, and yakṣa-rākṣasic,
and in which yuga their birth [occurs], and how long their lifespan is.

1.59.s:
yugeṣu yāstu jāyante prajāstā vai nibodhata.
āśurī sarpagopakṣipaiśācī yakṣarākṣasī.
yasmin yuge ca sambhūtistāsāṃ yāvattu jīvitam .. 59.1 ..
1.59.d:
युगेषु यास्तु जायन्ते प्रजास्ता वै निबोधत।
आशुरी सर्पगोपक्षिपैशाची यक्षराक्षसी।
यस्मिन् युगे च सम्भूतिस्तासां यावत्तु जीवितम् ॥ 59.1 ॥

1.59.s:
piśācāsuragandharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ.
yugamātrantu jīvanti ṛte mṛtyuvadhena te .. 59.2 ..
1.59.d:
पिशाचासुरगन्धर्वा यक्षराक्षसपन्नगाः।
युगमात्रन्तु जीवन्ति ऋते मृत्युवधेन ते ॥ 59.2 ॥
1.59.m: Piśācas, asuras, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents / live for the duration of a single yuga, except in the case of death by violence.

1.59.s:
mānuṣāṇāṃ paśūnāñca pakṣiṇāṃ sthāvaraiḥsaha.
teṣāmāyuḥ parikrāntaṃ yugadharmeṣu sarvaśaḥ .. 59.3 ..
1.59.d:
मानुषाणां पशूनाञ्च पक्षिणां स्थावरैःसह।
तेषामायुः परिक्रान्तं युगधर्मेषु सर्वशः ॥ 59.3 ॥
1.59.m: The lifespan of humans, domestic animals, and birds, along with immobile beings, / is measured entirely according to the conditions of the yuga.

1.59.s:
asthitistu kalau dṛṣṭā bhūtānāmāyuṣastu vai.
paramāyuḥ śatantvetanmanuṣyāṇāṃ kalau smṛtam .. 59.4 ..
1.59.d:
अस्थितिस्तु कलौ दृष्टा भूतानामायुषस्तु वै।
परमायुः शतन्त्वेतन्मनुष्याणां कलौ स्मृतम् ॥ 59.4 ॥
1.59.m: Instability in the lifespan of beings is indeed observed in the Kali [yuga]; / the maximum lifespan for humans in Kali is handed down as one hundred [years].

1.59.s:
devāsurapramāṇāttu saptasaptāṅgulaṃ hrasat.
ahgulānāṃ śataṃ pūrṇamaṣṭapañcāśaduttaram .. 59.5 ..
1.59.d:
देवासुरप्रमाणात्तु सप्तसप्ताङ्गुलं ह्रसत्।
अह्गुलानां शतं पूर्णमष्टपञ्चाशदुत्तरम् ॥ 59.5 ॥
1.59.m: Decreasing by seven fingers each from the stature of gods and asuras, / it is a full one hundred and fifty-eight fingers.

1.59.s:
devāsurapramāṇantaducchrāyaṃ kalijaiḥ smṛtam.
catvāraścāpyaśītiśca kalijairaṅgulaiḥ smṛtam .. 59.6 ..
1.59.d:
देवासुरप्रमाणन्तदुच्छ्रायं कलिजैः स्मृतम्।
चत्वारश्चाप्यशीतिश्च कलिजैरङ्गुलैः स्मृतम् ॥ 59.6 ॥
1.59.m: That height of the measure of gods and asuras is remembered [in contrast] to those born in Kali; / for those born in Kali, it is handed down as eighty-four fingers.

1.59.s:
svenāṅgulapramāṇena ūrddhvamāpādamastakam.
ityeṣa mānuṣotsedho hrasatīha yugāntike .. 59.7 ..
1.59.d:
स्वेनाङ्गुलप्रमाणेन ऊर्द्ध्वमापादमस्तकम्।
इत्येष मानुषोत्सेधो ह्रसतीह युगान्तिके ॥ 59.7 ॥
1.59.m:
By his own finger-breadth, upward from foot to head,
such is the human height; it diminishes here at the end of the yuga.

1.59.s:
sarveṣu yugakāleṣu atītānāgateṣviha.
svenāṅgulapramāṇena aṣṭatālaḥ smṛto naraḥ .. 59.8 ..
1.59.d:
सर्वेषु युगकालेषु अतीतानागतेष्विह।
स्वेनाङ्गुलप्रमाणेन अष्टतालः स्मृतो नरः ॥ 59.8 ॥
1.59.m:
In all yuga periods here, past and future,
measured by his own finger-breadth, a man is remembered as eight spans [in height].

1.59.s:
āpādato mastakantu navatālo bhavettu yaḥ.
saṃhatājānubāhustu sa surairapi pūjyate .. 59.9 ..
1.59.d:
आपादतो मस्तकन्तु नवतालो भवेत्तु यः।
संहताजानुबाहुस्तु स सुरैरपि पूज्यते ॥ 59.9 ॥
1.59.m:
One who is nine spans from foot to head,
with knees and arms well-knit, is worshipped even by the gods.

1.59.s:
gavāśvahastināñcaiva mahiṣa sthāvarātmanām.
krameṇaitena yogena hrāsavṛddhī yuge yuge .. 59.10 ..
1.59.d:
गवाश्वहस्तिनाञ्चैव महिष स्थावरात्मनाम्।
क्रमेणैतेन योगेन ह्रासवृद्धी युगे युगे ॥ 59.10 ॥
1.59.m:
For cattle, horses, elephants, buffaloes, and immovables,
decrease and increase occur yuga after yuga by this same order.

1.59.s:
ṣaṭsaptatyaṅgulotsedhaḥ paśūnāṃ kakudastu vai.
aṅgulāṣṭaśataṃ pūrṇamutsedhaḥ kariṇāṃ smṛtaḥ .. 59.11 ..
1.59.d:
षट्सप्तत्यङ्गुलोत्सेधः पशूनां ककुदस्तु वै।
अङ्गुलाष्टशतं पूर्णमुत्सेधः करिणां स्मृतः ॥ 59.11 ॥
1.59.m:
Seventy-six finger-breadths is the height of the hump of cattle;
one hundred and eight finger-breadths is remembered as the full height of elephants.

1.59.s:
aṅgulānāṃ sahasrantu catvāriṃśāṅgulaṃ vinā .
pañcāśataṃ hayānāñca utsedhaḥ śākhināṃ smṛtaḥ .. 59.12 ..
1.59.d:
अङ्गुलानां सहस्रन्तु चत्वारिंशाङ्गुलं विना ।
पञ्चाशतं हयानाञ्च उत्सेधः शाखिनां स्मृतः ॥ 59.12 ॥
1.59.m:
One thousand finger-breadths less forty [is the height] of horses,
and fifty is remembered as the height of trees.

1.59.s:
mānuṣasya śarīrasya sanniveśastu yādṛśaḥ.
tallakṣaṇastu devānāṃ dṛśyate tattvarśanāt .. 59.13 ..
1.59.d:
मानुषस्य शरीरस्य सन्निवेशस्तु यादृशः।
तल्लक्षणस्तु देवानां दृश्यते तत्त्वर्शनात् ॥ 59.13 ॥
1.59.m:
Just as the arrangement of the human body is,
similar characteristics are seen in the gods, according to the vision of reality.

1.59.s:
buddhyātiśayayuktañca devānāṃ kāyamucyate .
devānatiśayañcaiva mānuṣaṃ kāyamucyate .. 59.14 ..
1.59.d:
बुद्ध्यातिशययुक्तञ्च देवानां कायमुच्यते ।
देवानतिशयञ्चैव मानुषं कायमुच्यते ॥ 59.14 ॥
1.59.m:
The body of the gods is said to be endowed with superior intellect,
and the human body is said to fall short of the gods.

1.59.s:
ityete vai parikrāntā bhāvā ye divyamānuṣāḥ.
paśūnāṃ pakṣiṇāñcaiva sthāvarāṇāṃ nibodhata .. 59.15 ..
1.59.d:
इत्येते वै परिक्रान्ता भावा ये दिव्यमानुषाः।
पशूनां पक्षिणाञ्चैव स्थावराणां निबोधत ॥ 59.15 ॥
1.59.m:
Thus these states, divine and human, have been surveyed.
Now learn of cattle, birds, and immovable things.

1.59.s:
gāvo hyajā mahiṣyo'śvā hastinaḥ pakṣiṇo nagāḥ.
upayūktāḥ kriyāsvete yajñiyāsviha sarvaśaḥ .. 59.16 ..
1.59.d:
गावो ह्यजा महिष्योऽश्वा हस्तिनः पक्षिणो नगाः।
उपयूक्ताः क्रियास्वेते यज्ञियास्विह सर्वशः ॥ 59.16 ॥
1.59.m:
Cattle, goats, buffaloes, horses, elephants, birds, and trees—
these, when employed in every way in sacrificial rites here,

1.59.s:
devasthāneṣu jāyante tadrūpā eva te punaḥ .
yathāśayopabhogāstu devānāṃ śubhamūrttayaḥ .. 59.17 ..
1.59.d:
देवस्थानेषु जायन्ते तद्रूपा एव ते पुनः ।
यथाशयोपभोगास्तु देवानां शुभमूर्त्तयः ॥ 59.17 ॥
1.59.m:
are born again in the realms of the gods with the very same forms,
as objects of enjoyment according to wish, beings of auspicious form for the gods.

1.59.s:
teṣāṃ rūpānurūpaistaiḥ pramāṇaiḥ sthāṇujaṅgamaiḥ.
manojñaistattvabhāvajñaiḥ sukhino hyupapedire .. 59.18 ..
1.59.d:
तेषां रूपानुरूपैस्तैः प्रमाणैः स्थाणुजङ्गमैः।
मनोज्ञैस्तत्त्वभावज्ञैः सुखिनो ह्युपपेदिरे ॥ 59.18 ॥
1.59.m:
Through their appropriate forms and measurements, immovable and movable,
charming, knowing the true state of things, the fortunate have obtained [these].

1.59.s:
ataḥ śiṣṭān pravakṣyāmi sataḥ sādhūṃstathaiva ca.
saditi brahmaṇaḥ śabdastadvanto ye bhavantyuta.
sāyujyaṃ brahmaṇo'tyantaṃ tena santaḥ prajakṣyate .. 59.19 ..
1.59.d:
अतः शिष्टान् प्रवक्ष्यामि सतः साधूंस्तथैव च।
सदिति ब्रह्मणः शब्दस्तद्वन्तो ये भवन्त्युत।
सायुज्यं ब्रह्मणोऽत्यन्तं तेन सन्तः प्रजक्ष्यते ॥ 59.19 ॥

1.59.s:
daśātmake ye viṣaye kāraṇe cāṣṭalakṣaṇe .
na krudhyanti na hṛṣyanti jitātmānastu te smṛtāḥ .. 59.20 ..
1.59.d:
दशात्मके ये विषये कारणे चाष्टलक्षणे ।
न क्रुध्यन्ति न हृष्यन्ति जितात्मानस्तु ते स्मृताः ॥ 59.20 ॥
1.59.m:
Those who, regarding the ten-fold sense-object and the eight-fold inner organ,
neither grow angry nor rejoice, are remembered as self-conquered.

1.59.s:
sāmānyeṣu ca dharmeṣu tathā vaiśeṣikeṣu ca.
brahmakṣatraviśo yuktā yasmāttasmāddvijātayaḥ .. 59.21 ..
1.59.d:
सामान्येषु च धर्मेषु तथा वैशेषिकेषु च।
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशो युक्ता यस्मात्तस्माद्द्विजातयः ॥ 59.21 ॥
1.59.m:
Because Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas are intent
upon general duties and particular duties, they are therefore the twice-born.

1.59.s:
varṇāśrameṣu yuktasya svargagomukhacāriṇaḥ.
śrautasmārtasya dharmasya jñānāddharmaḥ sa ucyate .. 59.22 ..
1.59.d:
वर्णाश्रमेषु युक्तस्य स्वर्गगोमुखचारिणः।
श्रौतस्मार्तस्य धर्मस्य ज्ञानाद्धर्मः स उच्यते ॥ 59.22 ॥
1.59.m:
Of one intent upon the classes and stages of life, walking toward heaven and liberation,
that is called dharma through knowledge of the Vedic (*śrauta*) and traditional (*smārta*) dharma.

1.59.s:
vidyāyāḥ sādhanātsādhurbrahmacārī gurorhitaḥ.
kriyāṇāṃ sādhanāccaiva gṛhasthaḥ sādhurucyate .. 59.23 ..
1.59.d:
विद्यायाः साधनात्साधुर्ब्रह्मचारी गुरोर्हितः।
क्रियाणां साधनाच्चैव गृहस्थः साधुरुच्यते ॥ 59.23 ॥
1.59.m:
Through accomplishing learning and benefiting his teacher, a student is virtuous (*sādhu*);
and through accomplishing ritual acts, a householder is called virtuous.

1.59.s:
sādhanāttapaso'raṇye sādhurvaikhānasaḥ smṛtaḥ.
yatamāno yatiḥ sādhuḥ smṛto yogasya sādhanāt .. 59.24 ..
1.59.d:
साधनात्तपसोऽरण्ये साधुर्वैखानसः स्मृतः।
यतमानो यतिः साधुः स्मृतो योगस्य साधनात् ॥ 59.24 ॥
1.59.m:
Through accomplishing austerity in the forest, a Vaikhānasa is remembered as virtuous;
striving through accomplishing yoga, an ascetic is remembered as virtuous.

1.59.s:
evamāśramadharmāṇāṃ sādhanāt sādhavaḥ smṛtāḥ.
gṛhastho brahmacārī ca vānaprastho'tha bhikṣukaḥ .. 59.25 ..
1.59.d:
एवमाश्रमधर्माणां साधनात् साधवः स्मृताः।
गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी च वानप्रस्थोऽथ भिक्षुकः ॥ 59.25 ॥
1.59.m:
Thus, through accomplishing the duties of their stages of life, they are remembered as virtuous:
the householder, the student, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant.

1.59.s:
na ca devā na pitaro munayo na ca mānavāḥ.
ayaṃ dharmo hyayaṃ neti bruvanto'bhinnadarśanāḥ .. 59.26 ..
1.59.d:
न च देवा न पितरो मुनयो न च मानवाः।
अयं धर्मो ह्ययं नेति ब्रुवन्तोऽभिन्नदर्शनाः ॥ 59.26 ॥
1.59.m:
Neither the gods, nor the ancestors, nor the sages, nor mortals
have identical views when saying, 'This is dharma, and this is not.'

1.59.s:
dharmādharmāviha proktau śabdāvetau kriyātmakau.
kuśalākuśalaṃ karma dharmā dharmāviti smṛtau .. 59.27 ..
1.59.d:
धर्माधर्माविह प्रोक्तौ शब्दावेतौ क्रियात्मकौ।
कुशलाकुशलं कर्म धर्मा धर्माविति स्मृतौ ॥ 59.27 ॥
1.59.m:
Dharma and adharma are taught here as two words consisting of action;
skillful and unskillful deeds are remembered as dharma and adharma.

1.59.s:
dhāraṇā dhṛtirityarthāddhātordharmaḥ prakīrttitaḥ .
adhāraṇe'mahattve ca adharma iti cocyate .. 59.28 ..
1.59.d:
धारणा धृतिरित्यर्थाद्धातोर्धर्मः प्रकीर्त्तितः ।
अधारणेऽमहत्त्वे च अधर्म इति चोच्यते ॥ 59.28 ॥
1.59.m:
Dharma is proclaimed from the root meaning 'upholding' and 'maintaining';
and from non-upholding and unworthiness, it is called adharma.

1.59.s:
atreṣṭaprāpakā dharmā ācāryairupadiśyate.
vṛddhā hyalolupāścaiva ātmavanto hyadambhakāḥ.
samyagvinītā ṛjavastānācāryān pracakṣate .. 59.29 ..
1.59.d:
अत्रेष्टप्रापका धर्मा आचार्यैरुपदिश्यते।
वृद्धा ह्यलोलुपाश्चैव आत्मवन्तो ह्यदम्भकाः।
सम्यग्विनीता ऋजवस्तानाचार्यान् प्रचक्षते ॥ 59.29 ॥
1.59.m:
Here, the dharmas that secure what is desired are taught by teachers.
Those who are mature, free from greed, self-controlled, free from deceit,
well-disciplined, and upright—such men they call teachers.

1.59.s:
svayamācarate yasmādācāraṃ sthāpayatyapi.
ācinoti ca śāstrārthānyamaiḥ sanniyamairyutaḥ .. 59.30 ..
1.59.d:
स्वयमाचरते यस्मादाचारं स्थापयत्यपि।
आचिनोति च शास्त्रार्थान्यमैः सन्नियमैर्युतः ॥ 59.30 ॥
1.59.m:
Because he himself practices conduct (*ācāra*), establishes it,
and gathers the meanings of the treatises, endowed with restraints and observances [he is an *ācārya*].

1.59.s:
pūrvebhyo vedayitveha śrautaṃ saptarṣayo'bruvan.
ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni brahmaṇo'ṅgāni ca śrutiḥ .. 59.31 ..
1.59.d:
पूर्वेभ्यो वेदयित्वेह श्रौतं सप्तर्षयोऽब्रुवन्।
ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि ब्रह्मणोऽङ्गानि च श्रुतिः ॥ 59.31 ॥
1.59.m:
Having learned it from earlier ones here, the Seven Seers spoke the Vedic (*śrauta*) [lore]:
the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman verses, the limbs of the Veda, and revelation (*śruti*).

1.59.s:
manvantarasyātītasya smṛtvācāraṃ punarjagau.
tasmātsmārtaḥ smṛto dharmo varṇāśramavibhāgajaḥ .. 59.32 ..
1.59.d:
मन्वन्तरस्यातीतस्य स्मृत्वाचारं पुनर्जगौ।
तस्मात्स्मार्तः स्मृतो धर्मो वर्णाश्रमविभागजः ॥ 59.32 ॥
1.59.m:
Remembering the conduct of the past cosmic age of a Manu, he proclaimed it again;
therefore the dharma arising from the division of classes and stages of life is remembered as traditional (*smārta*).

1.59.s:
sa eṣa dvividho dharmaḥ śiṣṭācāra ihocyate.
śeṣaśabdāt śiṣṭa iti śiṣṭācāraḥ pracakṣyate .. 59.33 ..
1.59.d:
स एष द्विविधो धर्मः शिष्टाचार इहोच्यते।
शेषशब्दात् शिष्ट इति शिष्टाचारः प्रचक्ष्यते ॥ 59.33 ॥
1.59.m:
This twofold dharma is called the conduct of the cultured (*śiṣṭācāra*) here;
from the word 'remnant' (*śeṣa*), 'one who remains' (*śiṣṭa*) is derived, and thus it is called *śiṣṭācāra*.

1.59.s:
manvantareṣu ye śiṣṭā iha tiṣṭhanti dhārmikāḥ.
manuḥ saptarṣayaścaiva lokasantānakāraṇāt.
dharmārthaṃ ye ca śiṣṭa vai yāthātathyaṃ pracakṣyate .. 59.34 ..
1.59.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु ये शिष्टा इह तिष्ठन्ति धार्मिकाः।
मनुः सप्तर्षयश्चैव लोकसन्तानकारणात्।
धर्मार्थं ये च शिष्ट वै याथातथ्यं प्रचक्ष्यते ॥ 59.34 ॥
1.59.m:
The righteous who remain (*śiṣṭa*) in the cosmic ages of a Manu and abide here,
namely Manu and the Seven Seers, for the sake of the continuation of the world,
and those who remain for the sake of dharma, are described in their true nature.

1.59.s:
manvādayaśca ye śiṣṭā ye mayā prāgudīritāḥ.
taiḥ śiṣṭaiścarito dharmaḥ samyageva yuge yuge .. 59.35 ..
1.59.d:
मन्वादयश्च ये शिष्टा ये मया प्रागुदीरिताः।
तैः शिष्टैश्चरितो धर्मः सम्यगेव युगे युगे ॥ 59.35 ॥
1.59.m:
Manu and the others who were left, whom I mentioned before—
by those cultured ones dharma was practiced properly yuga after yuga.

1.59.s:
trayī vārtā daṇḍanītirijyā varṇāśramāstathā.
śiṣṭairācaryate yasmānmanunā ca punaḥ punaḥ.
pūrvaiḥ pūrvagatatvācca śiṣṭācāraḥ sa śāśvataḥ .. 59.36 ..
1.59.d:
त्रयी वार्ता दण्डनीतिरिज्या वर्णाश्रमास्तथा।
शिष्टैराचर्यते यस्मान्मनुना च पुनः पुनः।
पूर्वैः पूर्वगतत्वाच्च शिष्टाचारः स शाश्वतः ॥ 59.36 ॥
1.59.m:
Because the three Vedas, agriculture and trade, statecraft, sacrifice, and the classes and stages of life
are practiced by the cultured ones and by Manu again and again,
and because it has been observed by earlier and earlier beings, that conduct of the cultured is eternal.

1.59.s:
dānaṃ satyantapo'lobho vidyejyāprajanī dayā.
aṣṭau tāni caritrāṇi śiṣṭācārasya lakṣaṇam .. 59.37 ..
1.59.d:
दानं सत्यन्तपोऽलोभो विद्येज्याप्रजनी दया।
अष्टौ तानि चरित्राणि शिष्टाचारस्य लक्षणम् ॥ 59.37 ॥
1.59.m:
Giving, truthfulness, austerity, non-greed, learning, sacrifice, procreation, compassion—
these eight practices are the mark of the conduct of the cultured.

1.59.s:
śiṣṭā yasmāccarantyenaṃ manuḥ saptarṣayaśca vai.
manvantareṣu sarveṣu śiṣṭācārastataḥ smṛtaḥ .. 59.38 ..
1.59.d:
शिष्टा यस्माच्चरन्त्येनं मनुः सप्तर्षयश्च वै।
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु शिष्टाचारस्ततः स्मृतः ॥ 59.38 ॥
1.59.m:
Because the cultured ones, namely Manu and the Seven Seers,
practice it in all cosmic ages of a Manu, it is therefore remembered as the conduct of the cultured.

1.59.s:
vijñeyaḥ śravaṇāt śrautaḥ smaraṇāt smārtta ucyate.
ijyā vedātmakaḥ śrautaḥ smārto varṇāśramātmakaḥ.
pratyaṅgāni ca vakṣyāmi dharmasyeha tu lakṣaṇam .. 59.39 ..
1.59.d:
विज्ञेयः श्रवणात् श्रौतः स्मरणात् स्मार्त्त उच्यते।
इज्या वेदात्मकः श्रौतः स्मार्तो वर्णाश्रमात्मकः।
प्रत्यङ्गानि च वक्ष्यामि धर्मस्येह तु लक्षणम् ॥ 59.39 ॥
1.59.m:
It should be understood as *śrauta* from hearing (*śravaṇa*); it is called *smārta* from memory (*smaraṇa*).
*Śrauta* consists of sacrifice and the Veda; *smārta* consists of the classes and stages of life.
And I shall declare the subsidiary parts and the definition of dharma here.

1.59.s:
dṛṣṭvā prabhūtamarthaṃ yaḥ pṛṣṭo vai na nigūhati.
yathā bhūtapravādastu ityetatsatyalakṣaṇam .. 59.40 ..
1.59.d:
दृष्ट्वा प्रभूतमर्थं यः पृष्टो वै न निगूहति।
यथा भूतप्रवादस्तु इत्येतत्सत्यलक्षणम् ॥ 59.40 ॥
1.59.m:
He who, having seen an extensive matter, does not conceal it when questioned,
but speaks in accordance with fact—this is the mark of truthfulness.

1.59.s:
brahmacaryaṃ japo maunaṃ nirāhāratvameva ca.
ityetat tapaso mūlaṃ sughoraṃ taddurāsadam .. 59.41 ..
1.59.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं जपो मौनं निराहारत्वमेव च।
इत्येतत् तपसो मूलं सुघोरं तद्दुरासदम् ॥ 59.41 ॥
1.59.m:
Chastity, recitation of mantras, silence, and fasting—
this is the root of austerity, very terrible and difficult to approach.

1.59.s:
paśūnāṃ dravyahaviṣāmṛksāmayajuṣāṃ tathā.
ṛtvijāṃ dakṣiṇānāñca saṃyogo yoga ucyate .. 59.42 ..
1.59.d:
पशूनां द्रव्यहविषामृक्सामयजुषां तथा।
ऋत्विजां दक्षिणानाञ्च संयोगो योग उच्यते ॥ 59.42 ॥
1.59.m:
The combination of animals, material offerings, oblations, Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajus verses,
officiating priests, and sacrificial fees is called preparation (*yoga*).

1.59.s:
ātmavatsarvabhūteṣu yo hitāyāhitāya ca.
samā pravarttate dṛṣṭiḥ kṛtsnā hyeṣā dayā smṛtā .. 59.43 ..
1.59.d:
आत्मवत्सर्वभूतेषु यो हितायाहिताय च।
समा प्रवर्त्तते दृष्टिः कृत्स्ना ह्येषा दया स्मृता ॥ 59.43 ॥
1.59.m:
When an equal regard extends toward all beings as toward oneself,
whether for benefit or non-benefit, that in its entirety is remembered as compassion.

1.59.s:
ākruṣṭo'bhihato vāpi nākrośedyo na hanti vā.
vāṅ‌manaḥkarmabhiḥ kṣāntistitikṣaiṣā kṣamā smṛtā .. 59.44 ..
1.59.d:
आक्रुष्टोऽभिहतो वापि नाक्रोशेद्यो न हन्ति वा।
वाङ्‌मनःकर्मभिः क्षान्तिस्तितिक्षैषा क्षमा स्मृता ॥ 59.44 ॥
1.59.m:
One who, reviled or struck, does not revile in return or strike,
enduring through speech, mind, and deeds—this endurance is remembered as forbearance.

1.59.s:
svāminārakṣyamāṇānāmutsṛṣṭānāñca mṛtsu ca.
parasvānāmanādānamalobha iha kīrtyate .. 59.45 ..
1.59.d:
स्वामिनारक्ष्यमाणानामुत्सृष्टानाञ्च मृत्सु च।
परस्वानामनादानमलोभ इह कीर्त्यते ॥ 59.45 ॥
1.59.m:
Refraining from taking others' possessions, whether unguarded by their owner,
abandoned, or in the dirt, is proclaimed here as non-greed.

1.59.s:
maithunasyāsamācāro hyacintanamakalpanam.
nivṛttirbrahmacaryaṃ tadacchidraṃ dama ucyate .. 59.46 ..
1.59.d:
मैथुनस्यासमाचारो ह्यचिन्तनमकल्पनम्।
निवृत्तिर्ब्रह्मचर्यं तदच्छिद्रं दम उच्यते ॥ 59.46 ॥
1.59.m:
Non-indulgence in sexual intercourse, not thinking of it, and not imagining it—
that cessation is flawless chastity; it is called self-control.

1.59.s:
ātmārthaṃ vā parārthaṃ vā indriyāṇīha yasya vai.
na mithyā sampravartante śamasyai tattu lakṣaṇam .. 59.47 ..
1.59.d:
आत्मार्थं वा परार्थं वा इन्द्रियाणीह यस्य वै।
न मिथ्या सम्प्रवर्तन्ते शमस्यै तत्तु लक्षणम् ॥ 59.47 ॥
1.59.m:
For whom the senses do not operate wrongly,
either for one's own sake or for another's—that is the mark of tranquility.

1.59.s:
daśātmake yo viṣaye kāraṇe cāṣṭalakṣaṇe.
na krudhyettu pratihataḥ sa jitātmā vibhāvyate .. 59.48 ..
1.59.d:
दशात्मके यो विषये कारणे चाष्टलक्षणे।
न क्रुध्येत्तु प्रतिहतः स जितात्मा विभाव्यते ॥ 59.48 ॥
1.59.m:
He who, regarding the ten-fold sense-object and the eight-fold inner organ,
does not grow angry when thwarted, is recognized as self-conquered.

1.59.s:
yadyadiṣṭatamaṃ dravyaṃ nyāyenopāgatañca yat.
tattadguṇavate deyamityetaddānalakṣaṇam .. 59.49 ..
1.59.d:
यद्यदिष्टतमं द्रव्यं न्यायेनोपागतञ्च यत्।
तत्तद्गुणवते देयमित्येतद्दानलक्षणम् ॥ 59.49 ॥
1.59.m: Whatever wealth is dearest and lawfully obtained / should be given to a worthy person: this is the mark of giving.

1.59.s:
dānaṃ trividhamityetat kaniṣṭhajyeṣṭhamadhayamam .
tatra naiḥśreyasaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ svārthasiddhaye.
kāruṇyātsarvabhūtebhyaḥ suvibhāgastu bandhuṣu .. 59.50 ..
1.59.d:
दानं त्रिविधमित्येतत् कनिष्ठज्येष्ठमधयमम् ।
तत्र नैःश्रेयसं ज्येष्ठं कनिष्ठं स्वार्थसिद्धये।
कारुण्यात्सर्वभूतेभ्यः सुविभागस्तु बन्धुषु ॥ 59.50 ॥
1.59.m: Giving is threefold: lowest, highest, and intermediate. / Among these, that for the highest good is highest, that for one's own advantage is lowest, / [the intermediate is] out of compassion for all creatures, and equitable distribution among kin.

1.59.s:
śrutismṛtibhyāṃ vihito dharmo varṇāśramātmakaḥ.
śiṣṭācārāviruddhaśca dharmaḥ satsādhusaṅgataḥ .. 59.51 ..
1.59.d:
श्रुतिस्मृतिभ्यां विहितो धर्मो वर्णाश्रमात्मकः।
शिष्टाचाराविरुद्धश्च धर्मः सत्साधुसङ्गतः ॥ 59.51 ॥
1.59.m: The dharma prescribed by the Śruti and Smṛti, consisting of [the duties of] castes and stages of life, / not opposed to the conduct of the virtuous, is dharma shared by the good and righteous.

1.59.s:
apradveṣo hyaniṣṭeṣu tatheṣṭānabhinandanam.
prītitāpaviṣādebhyo vinivṛttirviraktatā .. 59.52 ..
1.59.d:
अप्रद्वेषो ह्यनिष्टेषु तथेष्टानभिनन्दनम्।
प्रीतितापविषादेभ्यो विनिवृत्तिर्विरक्तता ॥ 59.52 ॥
1.59.m: No aversion to what is disagreeable, likewise no rejoicing in what is agreeable, / turning away from attachment, torment, and despondency: this is detachment.

1.59.s:
saṃnyāsaḥ karmaṇo nyāsaḥ kṛtānāmakṛtaiḥ saha.
kuśalākuśalānāñca prahāṇaṃ tyāga ucyate .. 59.53 ..
1.59.d:
संन्यासः कर्मणो न्यासः कृतानामकृतैः सह।
कुशलाकुशलानाञ्च प्रहाणं त्याग उच्यते ॥ 59.53 ॥
1.59.m: Renunciation is the abandonment of ritual action, of things done along with things undone; / the discarding of both skilled and unskilled [actions] is called relinquishment.

1.59.s:
avyaktādyo'viśeṣācca vikāro'sminnacetane.
cetanācetānyatvavijñānaṃ jñānamucyate .. 59.54 ..
1.59.d:
अव्यक्ताद्योऽविशेषाच्च विकारोऽस्मिन्नचेतने।
चेतनाचेतान्यत्वविज्ञानं ज्ञानमुच्यते ॥ 59.54 ॥
1.59.m: From the unmanifest and the unparticularised arises transformation in this insentient [realm]; / the discernment of the difference between the sentient and insentient is called knowledge.

1.59.s:
pratyaṅgānāṃ tu dharmasya ityetallakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam .
ṛṣibhirdharmatattvajñaiḥ pūrve svāyambhuve'ntare .. 59.55 ..
1.59.d:
प्रत्यङ्गानां तु धर्मस्य इत्येतल्लक्षणं स्मृतम् ।
ऋषिभिर्धर्मतत्त्वज्ञैः पूर्वे स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे ॥ 59.55 ॥
1.59.m: This is remembered as the definition of the individual limbs of dharma / by the seers who know the truth of dharma in the previous cosmic age of the Svāyambhuva [Manu].

1.59.s:
atra vo varttayiṣyāmi vidhirmanvantarasya yaḥ .
itaretaravarṇasya cāturvarṇasya caiva hi.
pratimanvantarañcaiva śrutiranyā vidhīyate .. 59.56 ..
1.59.d:
अत्र वो वर्त्तयिष्यामि विधिर्मन्वन्तरस्य यः ।
इतरेतरवर्णस्य चातुर्वर्णस्य चैव हि।
प्रतिमन्वन्तरञ्चैव श्रुतिरन्या विधीयते ॥ 59.56 ॥
1.59.m: Here I shall relate to you the rule of the cosmic age of a Manu / concerning mutual caste and the fourfold caste system; / indeed, in every cosmic age of a Manu, a different Vedic scripture is laid down.

1.59.s:
ṛco yajūṣiṃ sāmāni yathāvat pratidaivatam.
ābhūtasaṃplavasyāpi varjyaikaṃ śatarudriyam .. 59.57 ..
1.59.d:
ऋचो यजूषिं सामानि यथावत् प्रतिदैवतम्।
आभूतसंप्लवस्यापि वर्ज्यैकं शतरुद्रियम् ॥ 59.57 ॥
1.59.m: The verses, the sacrificial formulas, and the chants, according to each deity, / until the cosmic flood of all beings, with the single exception of the Śatarudriya,

1.59.s:
vidhirhotraṃ tathā stotraṃ pūrvavatsampravartate.
dravyastotraṃ guṇastotraṃ karma stotraṃ tathaiva ca.
caturthamābhijanikaṃ stotrametaccaturvidham .. 59.58 ..
1.59.d:
विधिर्होत्रं तथा स्तोत्रं पूर्ववत्सम्प्रवर्तते।
द्रव्यस्तोत्रं गुणस्तोत्रं कर्म स्तोत्रं तथैव च।
चतुर्थमाभिजनिकं स्तोत्रमेतच्चतुर्विधम् ॥ 59.58 ॥
1.59.m: the ritual rule, the hotṛ's recitation, and the hymn of praise proceed as before. / Praise of material substance, praise of qualities, and likewise praise of deeds, / and the fourth is praise of noble birth: thus praise is fourfold.

1.59.s:
manvantareṣu sarveṣu yathā devā bhavanti ye.
pravarttayati teṣāṃ vai brahmastotraṃ caturvidham.
evaṃ mantraguṇānāñca samutpattiścaturvidhā .. 59.59 ..
1.59.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु यथा देवा भवन्ति ये।
प्रवर्त्तयति तेषां वै ब्रह्मस्तोत्रं चतुर्विधम्।
एवं मन्त्रगुणानाञ्च समुत्पत्तिश्चतुर्विधा ॥ 59.59 ॥
1.59.m: Whichever gods arise in all the cosmic ages of a Manu, / Brahmā sets in motion for them the fourfold praise; / thus the arising of the qualities of the mantras is fourfold.

1.59.s:
atharvayajuṣāṃ sāmnāṃ vedeṣviha pṛthak pṛthak .
ṛṣīṇāntapyatāmugrantapaḥ paramaduścaram .. 59.60 ..
1.59.d:
अथर्वयजुषां साम्नां वेदेष्विह पृथक् पृथक् ।
ऋषीणान्तप्यतामुग्रन्तपः परमदुश्चरम् ॥ 59.60 ॥
1.59.m: Separately for the Atharvan hymns, the sacrificial formulas, and the chants among the Vedas here, / as the seers practiced fierce and exceedingly difficult austerities,

1.59.s:
mantrāḥ prādurbabhūvurhi pūrvamanvantareṣviha.
paritoṣādbhayādduḥkhātsukhācchokācca pañcadhā .. 59.61 ..
1.59.d:
मन्त्राः प्रादुर्बभूवुर्हि पूर्वमन्वन्तरेष्विह।
परितोषाद्भयाद्दुःखात्सुखाच्छोकाच्च पञ्चधा ॥ 59.61 ॥
1.59.m: the mantras became manifest in previous cosmic ages of a Manu here / in five ways: from satisfaction, from fear, from grief, from joy, and from sorrow,

1.59.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ tapaḥkārtsnyena darśanena yadṛcchayā.
ṛṣīṇāṃ yadṛṣitvaṃ hi tadvakṣyāmīha lakṣaṇaiḥ .. 59.62 ..
1.59.d:
ऋषीणां तपःकार्त्स्न्येन दर्शनेन यदृच्छया।
ऋषीणां यदृषित्वं हि तद्वक्ष्यामीह लक्षणैः ॥ 59.62 ॥
1.59.m: through the entirety of the seers' austerities, through direct vision, and spontaneously. / The nature of being a seer among the seers I shall now declare by its marks.

1.59.s:
atītānāgatānāntu pañcadhā ṛṣirucyate.
atastvṛṣīṇāṃ vakṣyāmi hyārṣasya ca samudbhavam .. 59. 63 ..
1.59.d:
अतीतानागतानान्तु पञ्चधा ऋषिरुच्यते।
अतस्त्वृषीणां वक्ष्यामि ह्यार्षस्य च समुद्भवम् ॥ 59. 63 ॥
1.59.m: A seer is spoken of in five ways among those past and future; / therefore I shall tell of the seers and the origin of what pertains to seers.

1.59.s:
guṇasāmye varttamāne sarvasampralaye tadā.
aticāre tu devānāmatideśe tayoryathā .. 59.64 ..
1.59.d:
गुणसाम्ये वर्त्तमाने सर्वसम्प्रलये तदा।
अतिचारे तु देवानामतिदेशे तयोर्यथा ॥ 59.64 ॥
1.59.m: When the equilibrium of the qualities was present at the total dissolution then, / upon the transgression of the gods and their mutual transfer,

1.59.s:
abuddhipūrvakaṃ tadvai cetanārthaṃ pravarttate .
tena hyabuddhipūrvaṃ taccetanena hyadhiṣṭhitam .. 59.65 ..
1.59.d:
अबुद्धिपूर्वकं तद्वै चेतनार्थं प्रवर्त्तते ।
तेन ह्यबुद्धिपूर्वं तच्चेतनेन ह्यधिष्ठितम् ॥ 59.65 ॥
1.59.m: that [primal matter] proceeds without intention for the sake of the conscious [soul]; / therefore, though devoid of intention, it is presided over by the conscious one,

1.59.s:
varttate ca yathā tau tu yathā matsyodake ubhe.
cetanādhiṣṭhitaṃ tattvaṃ pravarttati guṇātmanā .. 59.66 ..
1.59.d:
वर्त्तते च यथा तौ तु यथा मत्स्योदके उभे।
चेतनाधिष्ठितं तत्त्वं प्रवर्त्तति गुणात्मना ॥ 59.66 ॥
1.59.m: and the two continue like fish and water. / The principle presided over by the conscious one operates through the nature of the qualities.

1.59.s:
karaṇatvāttathā kāryaṃ tadā tasya pravarttate.
viṣaye viṣayitvācca hyarthe'rthitvāttathaiva ca .. 59.67 ..
1.59.d:
करणत्वात्तथा कार्यं तदा तस्य प्रवर्त्तते।
विषये विषयित्वाच्च ह्यर्थेऽर्थित्वात्तथैव च ॥ 59.67 ॥
1.59.m: Because it is an instrument, its effect then proceeds / in the object from being an object, and likewise in purpose from having purpose.

1.59.s:
kālena prāpaṇīyena bhedāstu kāraṇātmakāḥ.
saṃsidhyanti tadā vyaktāḥ krameṇa mahadādayaḥ .. 59.68 ..
1.59.d:
कालेन प्रापणीयेन भेदास्तु कारणात्मकाः।
संसिध्यन्ति तदा व्यक्ताः क्रमेण महदादयः ॥ 59.68 ॥
1.59.m: By time, which brings things to fruition, the varieties consisting of causes / then succeed as manifest [entities] in due order, Mahat and the rest.

1.59.s:
mahataśvāpyahaṅkārastasmādbhūtendriyāṇi ca.
bhūtabhedāstu bhedebhyo jajñire te parasparam.
saṃsiddhikāraṇaṃ kāryaṃ sadya eva vivarttate .. 59.69 ..
1.59.d:
महतश्वाप्यहङ्कारस्तस्माद्भूतेन्द्रियाणि च।
भूतभेदास्तु भेदेभ्यो जज्ञिरे ते परस्परम्।
संसिद्धिकारणं कार्यं सद्य एव विवर्त्तते ॥ 59.69 ॥
1.59.m: From Mahat arose egoity, and from that the elements and senses; / the distinctions among the elements arose mutually from those distinctions. / The effect, which is the cause of attainment, transforms at once.

1.59.s:
yatholmukasruṭannūrddhvamekakālaṃ pravarttate.
tathā vivṛtaḥ kṣetrajñaḥ kālenaikena karmaṇā .. 59.70 ..
1.59.d:
यथोल्मुकस्रुटन्नूर्द्ध्वमेककालं प्रवर्त्तते।
तथा विवृतः क्षेत्रज्ञः कालेनैकेन कर्मणा ॥ 59.70 ॥
1.59.m: Just as a firebrand bursting upward operates at a single instant, / so the knower of the field is unfolded by a single action of time.

1.59.s:
yathāndhakāre khadyotaḥ sahasā sampradṛśyate.
tathā vivṛtto hyavyaktāt khadyota iva celvaṇaḥ .. 59.71 ..
1.59.d:
यथान्धकारे खद्योतः सहसा सम्प्रदृश्यते।
तथा विवृत्तो ह्यव्यक्तात् खद्योत इव चेल्वणः ॥ 59.71 ॥
1.59.m: Just as a firefly is suddenly seen in the dark, / so he is unfolded from the unmanifest, distinct like a firefly.

1.59.s:
sa mahān saśarīrastu yatraivāgre vyavasthitaḥ.
tatraiva saṃsthito vidvān dvāraśālāmukhe sthitaḥ .. 59.72 ..
1.59.d:
स महान् सशरीरस्तु यत्रैवाग्रे व्यवस्थितः।
तत्रैव संस्थितो विद्वान् द्वारशालामुखे स्थितः ॥ 59.72 ॥
1.59.m: That Mahat, possessing a body, stands just where he was situated at the beginning; / situated right there, the knowing one stands at the entrance to the hall of gates.

1.59.s:
mahāṃstu tamasaḥ pāre vailakṣaṇyādvibhāvyate .
tatraiva saṃsthito vidvāṃstamaso'nta iti śrutiḥ .. 59.73 ..
1.59.d:
महांस्तु तमसः पारे वैलक्षण्याद्विभाव्यते ।
तत्रैव संस्थितो विद्वांस्तमसोऽन्त इति श्रुतिः ॥ 59.73 ॥
1.59.m: Mahat is perceived beyond darkness because of his distinct nature; / situated right there, the knowing one is the end of darkness, so says the Śruti.

1.59.s:
buddhirvivarttamānasya prādurbhūtā caturvidhā .
jñānaṃ vairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ dharmaśceti catuṣṭayam .. 59.74 ..
1.59.d:
बुद्धिर्विवर्त्तमानस्य प्रादुर्भूता चतुर्विधा ।
ज्ञानं वैराग्यमैश्वर्यं धर्मश्चेति चतुष्टयम् ॥ 59.74 ॥
1.59.m: The intellect of the transforming one became manifest in four forms: / knowledge, dispassion, sovereign power, and dharma—this tetrad.

1.59.s:
sāṃsiddikānyathaitāni supratīkāni tasya vai .
mahataḥ saśarīrasya vaivarttyāt siddhirucyate .. 59.75 ..
1.59.d:
सांसिद्दिकान्यथैतानि सुप्रतीकानि तस्य वै ।
महतः सशरीरस्य वैवर्त्त्यात् सिद्धिरुच्यते ॥ 59.75 ॥
1.59.m: Now these innate [faculties] of his are beautifully formed; / through the transformation of that embodied Mahat, perfection is spoken of.

1.59.s:
atra śete ca yatpuryāṃ kṣetrajñānamathāpi vā.
purīśayatvātpuruṣaḥ kṣetrajñānāt saucyate .. 59.76 ..
1.59.d:
अत्र शेते च यत्पुर्यां क्षेत्रज्ञानमथापि वा।
पुरीशयत्वात्पुरुषः क्षेत्रज्ञानात् सौच्यते ॥ 59.76 ॥
1.59.m: Here, since he rests in the city, or else because he has knowledge of the field, / he is called puruṣa from lying in the city, and from knowing the field.

1.59.s:
kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetravijñānāt bhagavān matirucyate.
yasmādbuddhyā tu śete ha tasmādbodhātmakaḥ sa vai .
saṃsiddhaye parigataṃ vyaktāvyaktamacetanam .. 59.77 ..
1.59.d:
क्षेत्रज्ञः क्षेत्रविज्ञानात् भगवान् मतिरुच्यते।
यस्माद्बुद्ध्या तु शेते ह तस्माद्बोधात्मकः स वै ।
संसिद्धये परिगतं व्यक्ताव्यक्तमचेतनम् ॥ 59.77 ॥
1.59.m: The knower of the field is called the lord and intellect from his thorough knowledge of the field; / since he rests indeed with intellect, he is of the nature of awareness; / the insentient manifest and unmanifest is encompassed for the sake of [his] perfection.

1.59.s:
evaṃ nivṛttiḥ kṣetrajñā kṣetrajñenābhisaṃhitā.
kṣetrajñena parijñāto bhogyo'yaṃ viṣayastviti .. 59.78 ..
1.59.d:
एवं निवृत्तिः क्षेत्रज्ञा क्षेत्रज्ञेनाभिसंहिता।
क्षेत्रज्ञेन परिज्ञातो भोग्योऽयं विषयस्त्विति ॥ 59.78 ॥
1.59.m: Thus the cessation [of matter] is conceived by the knower of the field who knows the field: / 'This object of experience is fully known by the knower of the field.'

1.59.s:
ṛṣītyeṣa gatau dhātuḥśrutau satye tapasyatha.
etatsanniyate tasmin brahmaṇā sa ṛṣiḥ smṛtaḥ .. 59.79 ..
1.59.d:
ऋषीत्येष गतौ धातुःश्रुतौ सत्ये तपस्यथ।
एतत्सन्नियते तस्मिन् ब्रह्मणा स ऋषिः स्मृतः ॥ 59.79 ॥
1.59.m: The root ṛṣ- denotes going, hearing, truth, and austerity; / because he is directed toward this by Brahmā, he is remembered as a seer (ṛṣi).

1.59.s:
nivṛttisamakālaṃ tu buddhyāvyaktamṛṣiḥ svayam.
paraṃ hi ṛṣate yasmātparamarṣistataḥ smṛtaḥ .. 59.80 ..
1.59.d:
निवृत्तिसमकालं तु बुद्ध्याव्यक्तमृषिः स्वयम्।
परं हि ऋषते यस्मात्परमर्षिस्ततः स्मृतः ॥ 59.80 ॥
1.59.m: Simultaneously with cessation, the seer himself by his intellect / reaches (ṛṣate) beyond the unmanifest; because [he reaches] the supreme, he is remembered as a supreme seer (paramarṣi).

1.59.s:
gatyarthādṛṣaterddhātornāmanirvṛttirāditaḥ .
yasmādeṣa svayambhūtastasmāccātmarṣitā smṛtā.
īśvarāḥ svayamudbhūtā mānasā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ .. 59.81 ..
1.59.d:
गत्यर्थादृषतेर्द्धातोर्नामनिर्वृत्तिरादितः ।
यस्मादेष स्वयम्भूतस्तस्माच्चात्मर्षिता स्मृता।
ईश्वराः स्वयमुद्भूता मानसा ब्रह्मणः सुताः ॥ 59.81 ॥
1.59.m: From the root ṛṣ- meaning motion comes the formation of the word from the beginning; / since he is self-born, the status of self-seer (ātmarṣi) is remembered. / The lords, born of themselves, are the mind-born sons of Brahmā.

1.59.s:
yasmānna hanyate mānairmahān parigataḥ puraḥ.
yasmādṛṣanti ye dhīrā mahāntaṃ sarvato guṇaiḥ.
tasmānmaharṣayaḥ proktā buddheḥ paramadarśinaḥ .. 59.82 ..
1.59.d:
